rules.description: Rule id (`no-empty-catch`, or `plugin/rule`) to a level or a level with options.

accessor-order.description: `get` goes before `set` or `init`, and `add` before `remove`. The fix swaps the two accessors (not offered when a comment stands between or in them).

adjacent-overload-signatures.description: Overloads of one function or method (or call and construct signatures) with other members between them.

alpha-value-notation.description: The alpha value of `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `hwb()`, `lab()`, `lch()`, `oklab()`, `oklch()` or `color()` written as a number (`/ 0.5` is `/ 50%`); the comma form of `rgba()` and `hsla()` counts too.

ambiguous-block-association.description: A call without parentheses whose last argument is a call with a braces block (`expect { x }.to change { y }`, RuboCop Lint/AmbiguousBlockAssociation); also a `do` block that binds to the outer call while a block method such as `map` ends its arguments (`puts items.map do ... end`).

ambiguous-booleans.description: A plain `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `True`, `TRUE`, `False` or `FALSE` (in the usual casings): a boolean to YAML 1.1 parsers and a string to YAML 1.2 parsers. Lowercase `true` and `false` are fine.

allowed.description: Spellings that are not reported, for example `["on"]`.

check_keys.description: Also check mapping keys. Turn it off to keep GitHub workflow `on:`.

report_true_false.description: Also report `true` and `false` (unless listed in `allowed`), for code that wants every boolean quoted or spelled out.

ambiguous-variable-name.description: A variable, parameter or `global` name that is `l`, `O` or `I`.

and-or-is-not-if-else.description: A list `a && b || c` of three commands, unless `c` is `echo`, `printf`, `true`, `:`, `return` or `exit`.

apk-pin-versions.description: An apk add package without a version.

approved-verbs.description: A function named `Verb-Noun` whose verb is not in the list `Get-Verb` returns. Names without a dash are not checked.

apt-get-no-recommends.description: apt-get install that installs recommended packages.

apt-get-pin-versions.description: An apt-get install package without a version.

area-alt.description: The `alt` of an `<area>` is the name of the link in the image map; without an `href` it names nothing.

aria-hidden-body.description: `aria-hidden="true"` on `<body>` removes the whole page from the accessibility tree.

aria-label-misuse.description:
`aria-label` names interactive elements, landmarks and elements with a role. A generic element (`
`, ``, `

`, ``, ...) and an `` without `href` have no role to name.

array-in-string.description: A double-quoted argument that holds `$@` or `${array[@]}` among other text.

array-type-style.description: A declarator or parameter with C-style brackets after the name (Checkstyle ArrayTypeStyle).

array-without-index.description: `$BASH_SOURCE`, `$FUNCNAME` and the other bash arrays used with no subscript.

assert-false.description: An `assert` whose test is the literal `False`.

assert-tuple.description: An `assert` whose test is a tuple (a message written inside the parentheses).

assignment-not-seen.description: `var=value cmd "$var"`: `$var` is expanded before the assignment takes effect.

assignment-space.description: A command prefix `var= cmd` (reported at the start of the command), which sets `var` empty for the command; `var=value cmd` was probably meant.

async-suffix.description: An async method returning Task or ValueTask has a name that does not end in `Async`. Overrides, explicit interface implementations and `Main` are left alone (their names are not the method's to choose). Renaming needs the binding layer, so there is no fix.

at-rule-allowed-list.description: An at-rule (vendor prefix left out) that is not in the `list` option. An empty list allows everything.

list.description: The allowed at-rules, without `@`: names, or `/regex/`.

at-rule-disallowed-list.description: An at-rule (vendor prefix left out) that is in the `list` option.

list.description: The disallowed at-rules, without `@`: names, or `/regex/`.

at-rule-empty-line-before.description: An at-rule needs a blank line before it, unless a comment is right before it; the first at-rule of a block, and a blockless one right after a blockless one of the same name (`@import` lines), take none.

at-rule-no-unknown.description: An at-rule that no CSS specification lists. Vendor-prefixed ones are left out; SCSS has its own (`@include`, `@mixin`, ...), and Less at-rules are not checked. Tailwind's are left out by default.

at-rule-no-vendor-prefix.description: A vendor-prefixed at-rule that autoprefixer knows the standard one of.

attr-case.description: Attribute names are case-insensitive in HTML; lowercase is the convention. Everything inside `<svg>` and `<math>` keeps its case.

attr-delimiter.description: An attribute name and its value are joined by `=` without whitespace.

attr-pattern.description: An attribute name that does not match the `pattern` option (a regex; by default letters, digits, `-` and `:`, in either case).

pattern.description: The regex the value must match.

attr-quotes.description: An attribute value is quoted with `"`; it is quoted with `'` only when it holds a `"`. Unquoted values are reported too, except `name={expression}` in Svelte, where the braces are the syntax.

attr-spacing.description: A quoted attribute value is followed by whitespace before the next attribute.

attribute-allowed-values.description: An attribute that is limited to a list of values (`type` of `<button>`, `method` of `<form>`, ...) has another one.

attribute-boolean-style.description: A boolean attribute is true when present: `disabled`, not `disabled="disabled"`.

attribute-empty-style.description: An attribute whose empty value means the same as no value (`hidden`, `crossorigin`) is written without `=""`.

attribute-hyphenation.description: Vue's `attribute-hyphenation` (eslint-plugin-vue). Applies to components (a tag in PascalCase or with a hyphen), not to HTML and SVG elements.

attributes-order.description: Vue's `attributes-order` (eslint-plugin-vue) with its default order. A bare `v-bind="object"` takes the place of the attribute it precedes. Not sorted alphabetically.

backslash-separator.description: `build\out` is the pattern `buildout`: the backslash escapes `o`. Windows-style separators never match what was meant. Reported for a backslash before a letter, digit, `_` or `-` (`\.` and `\#` are ordinary escapes). No fix.

ban-ts-comment.description: `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-nocheck` before the first statement, and `@ts-expect-error` without a description of at least three characters in a comment (`@ts-check` is allowed).

banana-in-box.description: Angular's `banana-in-box` (@angular-eslint/template). `([x])` is no binding. Only in `.component.html` files.

bare-raise-outside-handler.description: A `raise` with no exception in code that no `except` clause of its function contains.

binary-operator-with-identical-operands.description: `x == x`, `a && a` and other comparison, logical and bitwise operators whose two sides are the same code (RuboCop Lint/BinaryOperatorWithIdenticalOperands).

block-no-empty.description: A rule or at-rule block with nothing in it, comments included.

boolean-literal-comparison.description: An equality with `true` or `false` (`x == true`, `x != False`) on either side (ruff E712, Checkstyle SimplifyBooleanExpression).

literals.description: The texts that are boolean literals

not_operators.description: Equality operators that are not a comparison of value (Python `is`)

boolean-symbol.description: The symbol `:true` or `:false`, which is probably meant to be the boolean (RuboCop Lint/BooleanSymbol).

break-outside-loop.description: A `break` that no loop of its function or class contains.

cached-method.description: A method decorated with `functools.lru_cache` or `functools.cache` (not a static method): the cache keeps `self` alive.

cd-without-exit.description: `cd`, `pushd` or `popd` whose failure is not handled (`cd dir || exit`). Not reported with `set -e`, for `cd ..` or `cd /`, or for `popd -n`.

class-naming.description: A class, interface or object whose name starts with a lowercase letter or an underscore (ktlint class-naming).

class-pattern.description: A class name that does not match the `pattern` option (a regex; by default kebab-case).

pattern.description: The regex the value must match.

collapsible-if.description: An `if` whose only statement is another `if`, neither having `elif` or `else`.

color-function-alias-notation.description: `rgba()` and `hsla()`, the legacy names of `rgb()` and `hsl()`.

color-function-notation.description: `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()` or `hsla()` with the legacy comma-separated arguments (`rgb(0, 0, 0)` is `rgb(0 0 0)`), also with a call such as `var()` as an argument.

color-hex-length.description: A hex color that can be written with three or four digits (`#aabbcc` is `#abc`); with the `style` option set to `long`, one that is written short.

style.description: `short` reports colors that can be shortened, `long` those that are short.

color-no-hex.description: A hex color: write a named color or a function instead.

color-no-invalid-hex.description: A hex color that does not have 3, 4, 6 or 8 hex digits.

commands-show-output.description: A fenced code block in which every line starts with `$ ` shows commands without their output, which makes copying them awkward (markdownlint MD014).

comment-space.description: A line comment has text right after its marker. Exempt: nothing but whitespace after the marker, a marker repeated (`////`, `##`), `--` separator lines, and a `#!` shebang on the first line. The fix inserts the space.

block.description: Also check block comments: text right after the opening or before the closing delimiter is reported (`/*a*/`). Exempt: an empty comment, and a delimiter repeated (`/**`, `/***/`). The fix inserts the space.

line.description: Check line comments (`// a`). Off, only block comments are checked (with `block`).

comment-syntax.description: A `//` comment where `#` is the convention (tflint terraform_comment_syntax). The fix writes `#`.

consistent-type-definitions.description: A type alias of an object type literal; write an `interface`.

consistent-type-imports.description: An import of a TypeScript file whose names are only used as types is written `import type`, and a type is not imported with `import("a")`. Names that are not used at all are left alone; the separate `import type` fix style is the only one.

constant-definition-in-block.description: A constant, class or module defined directly in a block (RuboCop Lint/ConstantDefinitionInBlock); `enums` blocks (Sorbet) are allowed.

constant-on-right.description: A comparison with the constant on the left: `null == x` is `x == null`, `1 < x` is `x > 1`. Without the type layer a constant is a literal, `nameof`, `int.MaxValue`-style member or an expression of those; a named constant on the left is not recognised.

constructor-summary-standard-text.description: The summary of a constructor starts with "Initializes a new instance of the <see cref="T"/> class" (struct), "Initializes static members of the ..." for a static constructor, and a private constructor may say "Prevents a default instance of the ... from being created". The `<see>` is compared with the name of the type. The fix puts the standard sentence before the text.

container-name-pattern.description: A `@container` name that does not match the `pattern` option (a regex). An empty pattern allows everything.

pattern.description: The regex a container name must match.

continue-outside-loop.description: A `continue` that no loop of its function or class contains.

copy-from-own-stage.description: A `COPY --from` that names the stage it is in.

copy-from-unknown-stage.description: A `COPY --from` that names no earlier stage: not a stage name, not the index of an earlier stage, and not an image (no `:`).

copy-instead-of-add.description: An ADD with no URL and no archive (`.tar`, `.gz`, `.tgz`, `.xz` and the like) among its arguments, which ADD would extract or download.

copy-many-needs-directory.description: A COPY with more than one source whose last argument does not end with `/`.

count-star.description: A `COUNT` of the constant 1 or 0 (sqlfluff CV04).

curly.description: The body of an `if`, `else`, loop or `when` entry is a statement without braces. Style `always` wants braces on every body; `chain` only on the branches of a chain where one has braces, spans lines or passes the line width, and on a loop body on its own line. `else if` is fine.

style.description: `always`: every body; `chain`: see the rule. The `style` row of the language's `curly_style` option overrides it in the formatter.

custom-media-pattern.description: A `@custom-media` name, without its `--`, that does not match the `pattern` option (a regex). An empty pattern allows everything.

pattern.description: The regex a custom media name, without its `--`, must match.

custom-property-no-missing-var-function.description: A custom property that the file declares, used in a value without `var()`. Properties that take names (`transition`, `will-change`, ...) are left out.

custom-property-pattern.description: A custom property, as declared, used in `var()` or named by `@property`, whose name without the `--` does not match the `pattern` option (a regex). An empty pattern allows everything.

pattern.description: The regex a custom property name, without its `--`, must match.

custom-type-var-return.description: A method whose `self` is annotated with a type variable that the return annotation repeats.

cyclic-needs.description: The `needs` of the jobs form a cycle, so no job of it can start.

datetime-utc-alias.description: `datetime.timezone.utc` (also imported as `timezone.utc`), for a target version that has `datetime.UTC` (3.11).

debug-assert-message.description: `Debug.Assert` without a message, or with a constant blank one. With the type layer the call is checked against `System.Diagnostics.Debug`; without it any call written `Debug.Assert` is. No fix.

debug-fail-message.description: `Debug.Fail` with a constant blank message. With the type layer the call is checked against `System.Diagnostics.Debug`; without it any call written `Debug.Fail` is. No fix.

declaration-block-no-duplicate-custom-pr.description: A custom property declared twice in one block (names are case sensitive); the repeat is reported.

declaration-block-no-duplicate-propertie.description: A property declared twice in one block; the earlier declaration is reported (the later one when only the earlier is `!important`). `src` and custom properties are left out.

ignore_consecutive_different_values.description: Leave a repeat right after the same property with another value alone (`display: -webkit-box; display: flex`).

declaration-block-no-shorthand-property-.description: A shorthand property declared after one of its longhands in the same block.

declaration-block-single-line-max-declar.description: A block written on one line with more declarations than the `max` option.

max.description: The most declarations a single-line block may have.

declaration-empty-line-before.description: A declaration right after a rule or at-rule needs a blank line before it, one after another declaration or first in a block takes none; a comment right before it, a single-line block, custom properties and variables are left alone.

declare-and-assign-separately.description: `export`, `local`, `declare`, `readonly` or `typeset` with a command substitution as the value reports the status of the declaration, not of the command.

default-except-not-last.description: A bare `except:` followed by another handler.

default-type-arguments.description: `Generator[X, None, None]` or `AsyncGenerator[X, None]`, for a target version where the arguments have defaults (3.13).

delete-apt-lists.description: A RUN that runs apt-get update (or apt update) and does not remove /var/lib/apt/lists, which stays in the image layer. A cache mount on that directory is fine.

deprecated.description: An element that HTML5 no longer has (`<center>`, `<font>`, `<marquee>`, ...).

deprecated-commands.description: A script uses a workflow command that GitHub has disabled (`::set-output`, `::save-state`, `::set-env`, `::add-path`); write to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, `$GITHUB_STATE`, `$GITHUB_ENV` or `$GITHUB_PATH` instead.

deprecated-import.description: An import from `typing_extensions` of a name that `typing`, `collections.abc` or `warnings` has in the target version, from `typing` of an alias of a `collections.abc` class, or of `List`, `Dict`, `Set`, `FrozenSet`, `Tuple`, `Type`.

deprecated-index.description: A list item read with the legacy dot syntax, `a.0` (tflint terraform_deprecated_index). The fix writes `a[0]`.

deprecated-interpolation.description: A string that is one interpolation, `"${var.a}"`, where the expression alone does (tflint terraform_deprecated_interpolation). The fix writes the expression. Not in Nomad job files (`.nomad`, `.nomad.hcl`), whose agent fills those in at run time.

except_in.description: Kinds of the parent (for example `Tuple`) whose strings are left alone. `Tuple`: only a string that is a whole argument is reported and unwrapped, as `terraform fmt` does.

deprecated-typing-alias.description: A subscript of `typing.List`, `Dict`, `Set`, `FrozenSet`, `Tuple` or `Type`, for a target version where the builtin is generic (3.9).

descriptive-link-text.description: Link text that is `click here`, `here`, `link` or `more` (markdownlint MD059).

destructor-summary-standard-text.description: The summary of a finalizer starts with "Finalizes an instance of the <see cref="T"/> class.". The `<see>` is compared with the name of the type. The fix puts the standard sentence before the text.

directive-keyword-space.description: No space between `#` and the directive keyword (`#if`, not `# if`).

distinct-group-by.description: `SELECT DISTINCT` in a query that has `GROUP BY`: the grouping already makes the rows distinct (sqlfluff AM01).

dnf-clean.description: dnf install with no dnf clean all after it.

doc-comment-space.description: A documentation line (`///`) starts with a single space. More spaces are allowed to indent continuation lines, not on the first line of the comment; a tab or no space is always reported.

doc-param-has-name.description: A `<param>` without a `name` attribute, or with an empty one. No fix.

doc-param-has-text.description: A `<param>` without text. Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.

doc-partial-required.description: A partial type or method without a documentation comment (or with an empty one). Each part is checked on its own; StyleCop (SA1601) accepts one documented part, which needs the other parts of the project. Which elements need documentation follows StyleCop's defaults: everything but private members.

doc-partial-summary-required.description: A documentation comment of a partial type or method without `<summary>` or `<content>` (and without `<inheritdoc />`). Each part is checked on its own. No fix.

doc-partial-summary-text.description: The `<summary>` (or `<content>`) of a partial type or method has no text. Each part is checked on its own. No fix.

doc-partial-typeparams.description: A documented partial generic type (with a `<summary>`) that has no `<typeparam>` for one of its type parameters. Each part is checked on its own. No fix.

doc-returns-has-text.description: A `<returns>` without text. Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.

doc-returns-required.description: A documented method or delegate that does not return `void` and has no `<returns>` (and no `<inheritdoc />`). Private members are left alone, as in StyleCop's defaults. No fix.

doc-summary-required.description: A documentation comment without `<summary>` (and without `<inheritdoc />`) on a type, member or field that StyleCop's defaults ask to document: everything but private members. Partial types and methods are `doc-partial-summary-required`. No fix.

doc-summary-text.description: A `<summary>` without text (`<summary></summary>`; `<summary />` is left alone, as StyleCop does). Partial types and methods are `doc-partial-summary-text`. No fix.

doc-text-ends-with-period.description: The last text of an element of a documentation comment does not end with a period (`.` or `.)`). Each paragraph of `<para>` and `<note>` is checked, a paragraph that ends in a colon (except the last), `-or-` and `<seealso>` are left alone, and an inline element (`<see />`, `<c>`, ...) at the end counts as not ending with a period. The fix adds the period, or replaces a trailing comma or semicolon with it.

doc-text-not-empty.description: A `<remarks>`, `<example>`, `<exception>` or `<permission>` element without text, written `<remarks></remarks>` or `<remarks />`. No fix.

doc-typeparam-has-name.description: A `<typeparam>` without a `name` attribute, or with an empty one, in the documentation of a generic class, struct, interface, method or delegate. No fix.

doc-typeparam-has-text.description: A `<typeparam>` without text (`<typeparam name="T" />` counts), in the documentation of a generic class, struct, interface, method or delegate. No fix.

doc-value-text.description: A property's `<value>` without text (`<value></value>`; `<value />` is left alone, as StyleCop does). Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.

doctype-html.description: A doctype other than `html` puts the browser in quirks or limited-quirks mode.

doctype-style.description: The doctype keyword is case-insensitive; uppercase is the convention.

document-end.description: A document without the `...` end marker (or, with `present: false`, one that has it).

present.description: `true` requires `...` after every document (fixable); `false` forbids it.

document-start.description: The first document does not start with `---`.

documented-outputs.description: An `output` block with no `description` argument (tflint terraform_documented_outputs).

documented-variables.description: A `variable` block with no `description` argument (tflint terraform_documented_variables).

duplicate-ids.description: Job ids that differ only in case (ids are case-insensitive; exact repeats are `no-duplicate-keys`), and step ids repeated within a job.

duplicate-stage-name.description: Two FROM instructions name their stage alike.

duplicate-table-alias.description: Two tables of one `FROM` clause with the same alias (or name when there is no alias) (sqlfluff AL04).

echo-in-substitution.description: A command substitution that only runs `echo` on words.

element-case.description: Element names are case-insensitive in HTML; lowercase is the convention. Everything inside `<svg>` and `<math>` keeps its case. Reported on the name of a start or end tag.

element-name.description: A custom element name is lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `.` and `_`, and has a `-`, so that it never clashes with an element HTML adds later. Everything inside `<svg>` and `<math>` is left alone.

element-required-attributes.description: An attribute the element must have (`lang` on ``, `src` on ``, `title` on `

empty-heading.description: Screen readers need text in a heading; whitespace is not text. An image with an `alt` or an `<svg>` inside counts as content.

empty-list-equality.description: A comparison with an empty list, `x == []` or `x != []` (tflint terraform_empty_list_equality): it is false for an empty set or a tuple of another type.

empty-section.description: A `[section]` header with nothing under it, usually left behind by a removed setting. Comments do not count as settings.

empty-statement.description: A `;` that is the body of an `if` or a loop, such as `while (x);` (Checkstyle EmptyStatement).

empty-title.description: The `<title>` names the page in the browser tab, search results and screen readers; whitespace is not text.

empty-when.description: A `when` with no statements and no comment (RuboCop Lint/EmptyWhen).

enum-entry-name-case.description: An enum entry whose name starts with a lowercase letter or an underscore (ktlint enum-entry-name-case).

enum-first-value-zero.description: The first value of an enum is not 0 (buf lint ENUM_FIRST_VALUE_ZERO). Proto3 and editions with open enums require it; proto2 files (also those with no `syntax`) are checked only with the `proto2` option.

proto2.description: Check proto2 files too, as buf does.

enum-no-allow-alias.description: `option allow_alias = true;` in an enum (buf lint ENUM_NO_ALLOW_ALIAS).

enum-pascal-case.description: An enum name that is not PascalCase (buf lint ENUM_PASCAL_CASE).

enum-value-prefix.description: An enum value does not start with the enum's name in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE and an underscore (buf lint ENUM_VALUE_PREFIX).

enum-value-upper-snake-case.description: An enum value name that is not UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (buf lint ENUM_VALUE_UPPER_SNAKE_CASE).

enum-zero-value-suffix.description: An enum value numbered 0 whose name does not end in `_UNSPECIFIED` (buf lint ENUM_ZERO_VALUE_SUFFIX with its default suffix).

eqeqeq.description: Angular's `eqeqeq` (@angular-eslint/template), on bindings, interpolations and block parameters. Only in `.component.html` files.

equals-hash-code.description: A class body that declares `boolean equals(Object)` and no `hashCode()`: equal objects get different hash codes (Checkstyle EqualsHashCode).

eval-array.description: An `eval` whose argument expands an array with `[@]`.

explicit-return-none.description: A `return None` in a function whose other returns (if any) return nothing or `None`, and that is not a generator. Left alone: a function that is only `return None`, a property, a function annotated with anything but `None`.

expose-port-range.description: An EXPOSE with a port above 65535.

f-string.description: A `"...".format(...)` on a string literal whose fields all name an argument.

f-string-missing-placeholders.description: An f-string with no replacement field in any of its parts.

fenced-code-language.description: A fenced code block without an info string (markdownlint MD040); name the language, or `text`.

field-lower-snake-case.description: A field name that is not lower_snake_case (buf lint FIELD_LOWER_SNAKE_CASE).

file-lower-snake-case.description: The file name (without `.proto`) is not lower_snake_case (buf lint FILE_LOWER_SNAKE_CASE).

file-name-matches-type.description: The file name, up to its first dot and ignoring case, is the name of the first type in the file; a generic type may also be written `Name{T,U}`. Not checked when that type is partial. No fix.

float-comparison.description: `==`, `!=`, `eql?` or `equal?` with a float on one side (a literal, `to_f`, arithmetic on a float), and a float in a `when` (RuboCop Lint/FloatComparison); comparing with 0 or `nil` is fine.

float-style.description: Restricts how plain floats are written. Every option is off until set: `.5` without a leading digit, `1e3` scientific notation, `.nan` and `.inf`. Quoted and tagged scalars are not checked. The fix for `.5` is `0.5`.

require_numeral_before_decimal.description: Report `.5`, `-.5e3`: a digit must come before the decimal point.

font-family-name-quotes.description: A quoted font family name that is also valid without quotes (`always-where-required`).

font-family-no-duplicate-names.description: The same family twice in one `font-family` list.

font-family-no-missing-generic-family-ke.description: A `font-family` (or `font`) list with no generic family (`serif`, `sans-serif`, ...) to fall back on. `@font-face` is left out.

forward-annotation-syntax-error.description: A quoted annotation that is not an expression.

from-first.description: An instruction other than ARG before the first FROM.

function-allowed-list.description: A function that is not in the `list` option. An empty list allows everything.

function-calc-no-unspaced-operator.description: `+` and `-` in `calc()` need whitespace on both sides, or the expression is invalid.

function-call-in-default.description: A call in the default of a parameter (not in a lambda, not a call of an immutable builtin such as `tuple`).

function-disallowed-list.description: A function that is in the `list` option.

function-linear-gradient-no-nonstandard-.description: A `linear-gradient()` that starts with a side (`top`) instead of `to top` or an angle.

function-name-case.description: A function name with capitals (`translateX` and the like keep theirs).

function-no-unknown.description: A function in a declaration value that no CSS specification lists. Not checked in SCSS and Less, whose built-in functions are not in the table.

future-feature-not-defined.description: A name imported from `__future__` that the module does not have.

gem-pin-versions.description: A gem install gem without a version.

generic-class.description: A class with `Generic[...]` among its bases, for a target version with type parameters (3.12).

generic-function.description: A function outside a class whose signature uses a module-level `TypeVar`, `ParamSpec` or `TypeVarTuple`, for a target version with type parameters (3.12).

get-attr-with-constant.description: `getattr(x, "name")` with a literal name that is an identifier (two arguments).

getter-return.description: A getter that does not return a value on every path, or has a `return;`.

go-pin-versions.description: A go install or get package without a version (or at latest).

hasattr-call.description: A call of `hasattr` or `getattr` that asks for `"__call__"`.

hash-compare-by-identity.description: A hash looked up with `x.object_id` as the key (`h[x.object_id]`, `key?`, `fetch`) (RuboCop Lint/HashCompareByIdentity).

heading-increment.description: A heading is more than one level deeper than the heading before it (an `h4` right after an `h2`). Going back up by any number of levels is fine (markdownlint MD001).

heading-level.description: Headings do not follow the document outline: the first heading is not an `<h1>`, a level is skipped going down the outline (`<h1>` then `<h3>`), or the page has a second `<h1>`.

heading-style.description: Headings are written in more than one style: `#` in front of the text (atx) or text over `===` or `---` (setext). Style `consistent` takes the first heading's. The fix rewrites a heading of one line, level 1 or 2.

kind.description: The name of the grammar kind of a heading node.

html-self-closing.description: Vue's `html-self-closing` (eslint-plugin-vue) with its defaults: HTML elements, components, SVG and MathML elements without content are self-closing, void HTML elements are not. The elements of the file's root (`<template>`, `<script>`) are left alone.

hue-degree-notation.description: The hue of `hsl()`, `hsla()`, `hwb()`, `lch()` or `oklch()` written as a number (`120` is `120deg`).

id-pattern.description: An `id` that does not match the `pattern` option (a regex; by default kebab-case: lowercase letters and digits in words joined by `-`, beginning with a letter).

pattern.description: The regex the value must match.

if-expr-with-false-true.description: A conditional expression with `False` and `True` arms.

if-expr-with-true-false.description: A conditional expression with `True` and `False` arms.

if-expr-with-twisted-arms.description: A conditional expression `b if not a else a`.

if-tuple.description: An `if` or `elif` whose test is a tuple.

if-with-same-arms.description: Two neighbouring branches of an `if`/`elif` chain with the same body.

implicit-alias.description: A table or column alias without the `AS` keyword (sqlfluff AL01, AL02).

implicit-concat-in-collection.description: An element of a list, tuple or set that is several string literals one after the other, without parentheses.

in-dict-keys.description: A membership test, `for` or comprehension over `.keys()` with no arguments.

ineffective-access-modifier.description: `private` or `protected` before `def self.name`, which it does not affect (RuboCop Lint/IneffectiveAccessModifier); `private_class_method :name` in the class makes the method private on purpose.

inherit-exception.description: A class that inherits `Exception` directly (`class A < Exception`, `Class.new(Exception)`) (RuboCop Lint/InheritException).

inheritdoc-on-inheriting-member.description: `<inheritdoc />` without `cref` on a type without a base list, or on a member that neither overrides nor implements anything (a constructor whose signature matches a base constructor is fine). No fix.

inline-comment.description: Gitignore-syntax files have no end-of-line comments: `*.log # logs` is the pattern `*.log # logs`, a file name with spaces and a `#`. No fix: put the comment on its own line.

input-missing-label.description: An `<input>` (not hidden or a button), `<select>` or `<textarea>` that no `<label>` names: it is not inside one, no `<label for>` points at its `id`, and it has no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

interpolation-check.description: A single-quoted string that holds `#{...}`, which would interpolate in double quotes (RuboCop Lint/InterpolationCheck).

invalid-escape-sequence.description: A backslash in a string that is not raw and does not start an escape sequence (`\d`, `\_`), also in the pieces of an f-string.

invalid-expression.description: A `${{ }}` expression that is not closed or empty, has unbalanced brackets or a string that is not closed, uses a character expressions do not have (such as a double quote), or names a context or function that does not exist.

invalid-job-id.description: A job id must start with a letter or `_` and contain only letters, digits, `-` and `_`.

invalid-property-value.description: A known EditorConfig or .NET property has a value it does not accept (`indent_style = tabs`, `dotnet_diagnostic.CA1000.severity = high`). Values are case-insensitive, `unset` is always valid, and .NET code-style options may end in `:silent`, `:suggestion`, `:warning` or `:error`; formatting options do not (Roslyn parses them with `bool.TryParse`, EditorConfigValueSerializer.cs). A trailing `# comment` is ignored, as Roslyn does. Unknown properties are not checked.

invalid-runs-on.description: A `runs-on` label that is not one of the known runner labels. A job that also has `self-hosted` is not checked; `${{ matrix.name }}` stands for the matrix's values, other expressions are skipped.

labels.description: Regular expressions; a label is valid when one matches all of it, ignoring case.

invalid-syntax.description: Code that Python rejects when it compiles the file, though the grammar allows it (a duplicate parameter, `nonlocal` at module level, `await` in a sync function, ...).

is-literal.description: An identity test (`is`, `is not`) with a string, bytes or number literal, a list, set, dict or comprehension, or a tuple of constants.

iterate-file-output.description: A `for` loop over the output of `cat`, `sort`, `sed`, `head` or `tail`.

iterate-find-output.description: A `for` loop over the output of `find`.

iterate-ls-output.description: A `for` loop over the output of `ls`.

json-cmd-entrypoint.description: A CMD, ENTRYPOINT or HEALTHCHECK CMD in shell form, which runs under `sh -c` and does not get signals.

key-name-casing.description: A key does not follow one of the allowed naming conventions. The checks are those of eslint-plugin-jsonc: a key with punctuation or whitespace never matches, `camelCase` also rejects `_` and `-`, `snake_case` and `kebab-case` reject capitals. No fix: renaming a key changes the data.

allowed.description: Accepted conventions: `camelCase`, `PascalCase`, `snake_case`, `kebab-case`, `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`. A key is fine when it matches one.

ignored_keys.description: Regular expressions; matching keys stay where they are and are not compared.

keyframe-block-no-duplicate-selectors.description: The same selector twice in one `@keyframes` rule (compared in lowercase).

keyframe-declaration-no-important.description: `!important` in a declaration of a `@keyframes` rule: the declaration is ignored.

keyframe-selector-notation.description: `from` and `to` in a `@keyframes` that also uses percentages (a block with nothing but keywords is left alone).

keyframes-name-pattern.description: A `@keyframes` name that does not match the `pattern` option (a regex). An empty pattern allows everything.

pattern.description: The regex a keyframes name must match.

lambda-assignment.description: A lambda assigned to a single name (an annotated one also in a class body is left alone).

last-user-not-root.description: A stage whose last USER is root (`root`, `0`, `root:group`, `0:group`).

layer-name-pattern.description: A `@layer` name that does not match the `pattern` option (a regex). An empty pattern allows everything.

pattern.description: The regex a layer name must match.

length-zero-no-unit.description: A zero length written with a unit (`0px`); other dimensions (`0s`, `0deg`) are left alone, and so is what is inside a function.

literal-in-interpolation.description: A number, symbol, `true`, `false`, `nil` or string literal as the whole content of a `#{...}` (RuboCop Lint/LiteralInInterpolation).

long-title.description: Search engines cut a title off after about 70 characters.

map-dup-name.description: A `<map>` whose `name` an earlier `<map>` already has: `usemap` finds the first.

max-body-length.description: A rule whose recipe has more lines than allowed (checkmake `maxbodylength`). Every physical line counts, a continued command and a tab-indented comment included.

max.description: The most lines a recipe may have.

max-line-length.description: A line is longer than the configured number of characters.

allow_non_breakable_inline_mappings.description: With `allow_non_breakable_words`, also do not report a `key: value` line whose value has no space. Only in languages that have such lines (YAML).

allow_non_breakable_words.description: Do not report a line that has no space after its indentation (and after a leading `#` run or `- `), such as a long URL.

max-nesting-depth.description: A rule or at-rule nested in more rules or at-rules than the `max` option.

media-feature-name-allowed-list.description: A media feature that is not in the `list` option. An empty list allows everything.

list.description: The allowed media features: names, or `/regex/`.

media-feature-name-disallowed-list.description: A media feature that is in the `list` option.

list.description: The disallowed media features: names, or `/regex/`.

media-feature-name-no-unknown.description: A media feature name in `@media` that is not a CSS one. Vendor-prefixed names are left out.

member-order.description: Members are out of order. Compared with the member before, in the order of the `element_order` option: the kind (fields, constructors, finalizers, delegates, events, enums, interfaces, properties, indexers, operators, methods, structs, classes; in a namespace or file: namespaces, delegates, enums, interfaces, structs, classes), the access (public, internal, protected internal, protected, private protected, private), constants before other fields, static before instance members, readonly fields before the others. A trait only counts between members that agree on the traits listed before it. No fix: moving members would have to take their comments and directives along.

element_order.description: The traits that decide the order, most important first. A trait that is left out is not checked.

merge-consecutive-run.description: A RUN that is a single command, directly after another single-command RUN with the same flags (a comment in between does not count).

message-pascal-case.description: A message name that is not PascalCase (buf lint MESSAGE_PASCAL_CASE).

meta-refresh.description: `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="5">` reloads or redirects after a delay, which disorients screen reader users and cannot be paused. A delay of 0 is allowed.

min-phony.description: A target that must exist and be declared `.PHONY` (checkmake `minphony`). Reported on the last `.PHONY` line, or the last rule's when there is none.

required.description: The targets every Makefile must declare `.PHONY`.

missing-doctype.description: A document without a doctype is rendered in quirks mode.

missing-permissions.description: A job without `permissions`, in a workflow without top-level `permissions`: it gets the repository's default token permissions, often write access.

missing-super.description: `initialize` of a class with a parent other than Object, and the lifecycle callbacks `inherited` and `method_added`, that do not call `super` (RuboCop Lint/MissingSuper).

mixed-regexp-capture-types.description: A regexp literal that has both `(?<name>...)` and plain `(...)` groups (RuboCop Lint/MixedRegexpCaptureTypes).

modifier-order.description: The modifiers of a declaration are not in the order the style wants (Java: `public protected private abstract default static sealed non-sealed final transient volatile synchronized native strictfp`; Kotlin: ktlint's order). The fix puts them in order.

module-import-not-at-top-of-file.description: An import at module level after code (docstrings, `__all__`, blocks, and `sys.path` or `os.environ` setup are not code).

multiple-labeled-controls.description: A `<label>` without `for` that holds more than one control: it labels only the first.

multiple-starred-expressions.description: An assignment target with two starred names.

multiple-starts-ends-with.description: `a.startswith(x) or a.startswith(y)` (also `endswith`): the methods take a tuple.

multiple-statements-on-one-line-colon.description: A compound statement whose body starts on the line of its colon (not `def`, not a lone `...`).

mutable-argument-default.description: A parameter whose default is a list, dict or set (literal, comprehension or `list()`, `dict()`, `set()`, `collections.deque()`, ...), unless its annotation is an immutable type.

mutable-class-default.description: A class attribute assigned a list, dict, set or comprehension (or a call that builds one) without a `ClassVar` or `Final` annotation; data classes, Pydantic models and named tuples are left alone.

name-pattern.description: The `name` of a form control that does not match the `pattern` option (a regex; by default camelCase, with a trailing `[]` allowed).

pattern.description: The regex the value must match.

named-grid-areas-no-invalid.description: A `grid-template-areas` whose rows differ in length, are empty, or hold an area that is not a rectangle.

naming-convention.description: A name does not follow the style set for what it names: operations, fragments, variables, fields, arguments, types, enum values and directives. `PascalCase` and `camelCase` allow letters and digits only, `snake_case` and `UPPER_CASE` forbid the other case; leading underscores are ignored. No fix: renaming changes the schema or the queries that use it. Equivalent: graphql-eslint naming-convention (styles only, no prefix or suffix lists).

arguments.description: Style of argument names in definitions.

fields.description: Style of field and input field names in definitions.

needless-bool.description: An `if` that returns `True` (or `False`) and is followed, or continued by `else`, by the opposite boolean.

negation-of-excluded-parent.description: Git cannot re-include a file when a parent directory is excluded: `!a/b` after `a/` has no effect. Exclude the contents (`a/*`) instead. Not reported in `.dockerignore`, where the later pattern wins. Only literal paths are checked.

nested-with.description: A `with` whose only statement is another `with` (both sync or both async).

no-abstract-role.description: Abstract roles (`widget`, `landmark`, `command`, ...) are for the ARIA taxonomy, not for authors.

no-alt-text.description: An image with empty alternate text, `![](url)` (markdownlint MD045).

no-anonymous-operations.description: An operation without a name (`{ a }`, `query { a }`), which tools that log, trace or cache by operation name cannot tell apart. Equivalent - graphql-eslint no-anonymous-operations.

no-assignment-in-condition.description: The condition of an `if`, ternary or loop is an assignment not wrapped in parentheses of its own (ESLint no-cond-assign, PHPCS Generic.CodeAnalysis.AssignmentInCondition). Python's `:=` is the idiom and is left alone.

no-assignment-in-logical-condition.description: `if a && b = c`: the condition is a logical operation whose right operand is an assignment not wrapped in parentheses (RuboCop Lint/AssignmentInCondition); a plain assignment condition is `no-assignment-in-condition`.

no-async-promise-executor.description: `new Promise(async ...)`: an error thrown in the executor is lost.

no-at-debug-tags.description: Svelte's `no-at-debug-tags` (eslint-plugin-svelte). The tag pauses the browser's debugger when its values change.

no-at-html-tags.description: Svelte's `no-at-html-tags` (eslint-plugin-svelte). Escape the text or sanitize it before it is rendered, or turn the rule off for a value you control.

no-automatic-variable-assignment.description: An assignment to, a parameter named like, or a `foreach` variable named like an automatic variable (`$Error`, `$Event`, `$input`, `$PSItem`, `$_`, `$PWD`, `$Host`, `$this`, `$true`, ...). `$null = ...` is fine.

no-autoplay.description: Autoplaying audio and video annoys users and fails accessibility guidelines; `muted` media is allowed.

no-backticks.description: A command substitution written with backticks.

no-bare-urls.description: A URL that is neither a link nor an autolink (markdownlint MD034), found when it follows a space or starts the paragraph. Reported on the URL.

no-broad-catch.description: A `catch`, `except` or `rescue` that catches everything (`bare`), or one of the broad `types` and does not raise the error again and has no call matching `handled` (ruff E722 and BLE001, RuboCop Lint/RescueException). A language sets what is broad in its grammar's `rule` row.

bare.description: A clause with no type is broad

handled.description: A call that handles the error (logs its traceback)

no-case-declarations.description: `let`, `const`, a function or a class declared directly in a `case` clause, where it is visible to the other cases.

no-class-assign.description: A class declared by name that is assigned to.

no-cmdlet-aliases.description: A command written with one of the default aliases of Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7 (`gci`, `ls`, `%`, `?`, `iex`, ...). The table is the one of a Windows host; PSScriptAnalyzer reads the aliases of the host it runs on.

no-comment-before-block.description: A comment between the head of an `if`, `else`, `while`, `do`, `for`, `foreach`, `lock`, `try`, `catch`, `finally`, `switch`, `checked` or `unchecked` and its `{`. Put it inside the block or above the statement.

no-conditional-comment.description: An Internet Explorer conditional comment (`<!--[if IE]>`). Only IE 9 and older read them; other browsers see a comment.

no-const-assign.description: A `const` variable that is assigned to again (the initializer is not).

no-constant-comparison.description: An equality or comparison of two literals (ruff PLR0133, ESLint no-constant-binary-expression).

no-constant-condition.description: The condition of an `if`, ternary or loop is a literal, so one branch never runs (ESLint no-constant-condition, PHPCS Generic.CodeAnalysis.UnconditionalIfStatement). `while (true)` and `while (1)` are the usual endless loop and are left alone.

no-control-regex.description: A control character (below U+0020) in the constant string given to `new Regex(...)` and the static methods of `Regex`, written raw or as an escape.

no-copy-whole-stage.description: A `COPY --from` with `/` as a source and as the target.

no-debugger.description: A debugger statement, a call of one of the `calls` that start a debugger or an import matching `imports` (ESLint no-debugger, ruff T100); a language lists its calls in its grammar's `rule` row.

imports.description: An import of a debugger module

no-default-summary.description: A `<summary>` that starts with the text Visual Studio generates, "Summary description for ...". Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.

no-default-true-switch.description: A `[switch]` parameter with the default value `$true`.

no-default-value-type-constructor.description: `new S()` of a value type with an implicit parameterless constructor and no initializer: write `default(S)` (`Guid.Empty`, `CancellationToken.None`, `IntPtr.Zero`, the enum member with value 0 where they exist). No fix for a target-typed `new()`.

no-deprecated-attr.description: An attribute that HTML5 no longer has on that element (`align`, `bgcolor`, `border`, ...).

no-deprecated-html-element-is.description: Vue's `no-deprecated-html-element-is` (eslint-plugin-vue). Only in `.vue` files, where a plain `is` would make a customized built-in element.

no-deprecated-slot-attribute.description: Vue's `no-deprecated-slot-attribute` (eslint-plugin-vue). Only in `.vue` files, because in HTML `slot` assigns an element to a web component's slot.

no-descending-specificity.description: A rule whose selector ends in the same compound (without its pseudo-classes) as an earlier rule in the same at-rule and has a lower specificity: the earlier one wins where the later was meant to. Nested rules are not compared.

no-doc-placeholder.description: A `<placeholder>` element in a documentation comment. No fix.

no-doc-slashes-in-plain-comment.description: A `///` comment that holds only text, no XML element: a plain comment written with documentation slashes. The fix writes `//`, unless the comment documents a declaration (it would remove documentation).

no-dupe-class-members.description: A class member declared twice (a getter and a setter may share one, a static and an instance member may not clash).

no-dupe-else-if.description: An `else if` condition that an earlier condition of the chain already covers.

no-dupe-keys.description: Vue's `no-dupe-keys` (eslint-plugin-vue). A name defined twice in `props`, `computed`, `data`, `methods` and `setup` of a component object; or a prop or `defineModel` of `<script setup>` that a top-level name of the script (a `const`, a function, an import) repeats, unless that name reads from the props object (`const a = props.a`, `toRef(props, 'a')`).

no-dupe-on-directives.description: Svelte's `no-dupe-on-directives` (eslint-plugin-svelte). The same event and handler twice (modifiers do not count); both directives are reported.

no-dupe-style-properties.description: Svelte's `no-dupe-style-properties` (eslint-plugin-svelte). `|important` is not part of the property.

no-dupe-v-else-if.description: Vue's `no-dupe-v-else-if` (eslint-plugin-vue). Conditions are compared as text without blanks, `||` alternatives one by one; a condition that only some earlier `&&` terms cover is not found.

no-duplicate-anchors.description: An anchor name is defined again in the same document; an alias refers to the latest definition above it, which is easy to misread.

no-duplicate-at-import-rules.description: The same `@import` (url and media list) twice in one file.

no-duplicate-case.description: Two arms of one `switch` (or `match`, `when`, `case`) have the same test; the second arm can never run. ESLint `no-duplicate-case`.

no-duplicate-class.description: A class name written twice in one `class` attribute.

no-duplicate-doc-text.description: Two elements of one documentation comment with the same text (a copied and pasted `<param>`, for example). Empty elements and "The parameter is not used." are ignored. No fix.

no-duplicate-enum-values.description: Two members of one enum initialized with the same string or number.

no-duplicate-heading.description: Two headings have the same text (markdownlint MD024), which makes their anchors ambiguous.

no-duplicate-id.description: An `id` that an earlier element of the document already has. Ids must be unique: scripts, links and labels find the first element only. Empty ids are left alone.

no-duplicate-include.description: An element of a project file (`PackageReference`, `ProjectReference`, `Compile`, ...) has the same `Include` as an earlier element of the same name in the same parent. The duplicate is a restore warning or a build error.

no-duplicate-keys.description: A mapping has the same key twice (after decoding escapes and quotes); parsers disagree on which value wins.

merge_keys.description: Languages with a merge key (YAML `<<`) only. `allow` skips merge keys, which may repeat; `forbid` reports a second one like any other duplicate key.

no-duplicate-pattern.description: The same pattern appears twice with no opposite pattern (`!x` for `x`) in between, so the second one changes nothing.

no-duplicate-sections.description: Two sections of one file have the same name (EditorConfig: glob). Readers merge them or keep only one, so the settings of the other may be lost; merge them.

no-duplicate-selectors.description: The same selector list (in any order) on two rules in one block or file.

no-else-return.description: An `else` after an `if` chain whose branches all end in `return`: the code of the `else` can follow the `if`. An `else if` is left alone (ESLint `allowElseIf`).

no-emphasis-as-heading.description: A one-line paragraph that is only emphasized text without closing punctuation (markdownlint MD036); use a heading.

no-empty-attribute-parens.description: An attribute with empty parentheses: `[Foo()]` is `[Foo]`. Parentheses with a comment in them are left alone.

no-empty-block.description: A block with no statement and no comment, as the body of an `if`, `else`, loop, `try` or `finally` (also when the language wraps the block in a node of its own; an empty `catch` is `no-empty-catch`) (ESLint no-empty, Checkstyle EmptyBlock, PHPCS Generic.CodeAnalysis.EmptyStatement).

no-empty-catch.description: A `catch`, `except` or `rescue` clause whose body has no statement (a lone `pass` counts as none) and no comment, so the error is silently ignored (ESLint no-empty, Checkstyle EmptyCatchBlock, ruff S110, RuboCop Lint/SuppressedException). With `comment_handles` off a comment does not count (PSScriptAnalyzer). With `broad_only` only a clause that catches everything or one of the `types` is reported.

broad_only.description: Report only a clause that catches everything or a broad type

comment_handles.description: A comment in the body counts as handling the error

no-empty-character-class.description: `[]` in a regex literal, which matches nothing.

no-empty-class-body.description: A class or interface with `{ }` and nothing in it (ktlint no-empty-class-body).

no-empty-comment.description: A comment has no text. A block comment is reported wherever it is; an empty line comment only when it begins or ends a run of comments, because a bare `//` between two comment lines separates paragraphs.

no-empty-delegate-parens.description: An anonymous method with an empty parameter list: `delegate() { }` is `delegate { }`. Parentheses with a comment in them are left alone. The fix is unsafe: without a parameter list the method also converts to delegate types that have parameters, which can change which overload is chosen.

no-empty-file.description: A `.kt` file with nothing in it but a package, imports and comments (ktlint no-empty-file).

no-empty-keys.description: A key is empty or only whitespace (after decoding escapes); some consumers cannot address such a property.

no-empty-links.description: A link whose destination is empty or only `#` (markdownlint MD042).

no-empty-object-type.description: The type `{}` (not in an intersection) and an interface with no members and at most one `extends`.

no-empty-pattern.description: A destructuring pattern with nothing in it (`{}`, `[]`).

no-empty-source.description: A file with nothing but whitespace (a file with only comments is not empty).

no-empty-statement.description: A lone `;` is a statement that does nothing. A statement labelled `label: ;` is allowed. The fix removes the statement (its whole line when it is alone on it), or turns an empty loop or `if` body into `{ }`; it is not offered for the only statement of a switch section. Overlaps compiler CS0642 for `if (x);`.

no-empty-values.description: A mapping key or sequence entry without a value (an implicit null). Values with an anchor or tag are not empty. Reported at the `:` or `-`.

no-eval.description: A call of one of the `calls` that run a string as code (ruff S102, ESLint no-eval); a language lists its calls in its grammar's `rule` row.

calls.description: Calls that run a string as code

no-extra-boolean-cast.description: `!!x` or `Boolean(x)` where the value is used as a boolean anyway (a condition, `!`, `Boolean(...)`).

no-fallthrough.description: A `case` with statements that can reach the next `case` or `default`, or an empty one followed by a blank line, without a comment that says `falls through` before the next one (or at the end of its block).

no-floating-package-version.description: A `PackageReference` (or `PackageVersion`) whose `Version` contains `*` restores a different package as new versions appear. Reported on the attribute; no fix, because the version to pin is a decision.

no-flow-mappings.description: A flow mapping (`{a: 1}`); write a block mapping instead.

no-flow-sequences.description: A flow sequence (`[a, b]`); write a block sequence instead.

no-from-platform.description: A FROM with a fixed `--platform`; a variable such as `$BUILDPLATFORM` is fine.

no-func-assign.description: A function declared by name that is assigned to.

no-global-vars.description: A variable in the `global:` scope, other than the special variables PSScriptAnalyzer exempts (`$global:LASTEXITCODE`, `$global:ErrorActionPreference`, `$global:PSDefaultParameterValues`, ...).

no-implicit-button-type.description: A `<button>` without a `type` is a submit button, which is rarely meant outside a form. A Svelte spread (`{...props}`) may carry the `type`.

no-implicit-close.description:
An element whose end tag is left out is closed by the next sibling or its parent's end tag (`
  • `, `

    `, ...). Writing the end tag says where it ends. Void and self-closed elements have none.

no-implicit-input-type.description: An `<input>` without a `type` is a text field by default; writing the type says so.

no-import-assign.description: An imported binding that is assigned to, and the members of a namespace import (`import * as ns`) that are assigned to, deleted or passed to `Object.assign` and the like.

no-inferrable-types.description: A type annotation of a variable, parameter or property that its initial value already gives (`const a: number = 5`; not `readonly` or optional properties).

no-inline-html.description: Raw HTML in a document (markdownlint MD033). Comments are not reported. Reported once per HTML block, not per tag.

no-inline-style.description: A `style` attribute is a sign of unstructured CSS. `display` alone is allowed, because scripts toggle it. A Svelte `style:property` directive is one too.

no-interactive-commands.description: A RUN that calls ssh, vim, shutdown, service, ps, free, top, kill or mount.

no-invalid-double-slash-comments.description: A rule or declaration that starts with `//`: CSS has no line comments, so the text swallows the statement.

no-invalid-position-at-import-rule.description: An `@import` after a rule that is not `@charset`, `@layer` or another `@import`: the browser ignores it.

no-invalid-position-declaration.description: A declaration at the top of a file, or in an at-rule such as `@media` that is not inside a rule.

no-irregular-whitespace.description: A no-break space, zero-width space or other unusual whitespace character outside a string.

no-latest-tag.description: A FROM image tagged `latest` (without a digest).

no-lone-template.description: Vue's `no-lone-template` (eslint-plugin-vue). A nested `<template>` is a wrapper that Vue drops, so it only makes sense with a directive. Only in `.vue` files.

no-lonely-if.description: An `if` that is the only statement of an `else` block: write `else if`.

no-loss-of-precision.description: A number literal that the double it becomes cannot represent exactly.

no-misleading-backtick.description: A backtick that is followed by blanks before the end of the line, so it does not continue the line.

no-misleading-character-class.description: A character class in the constant string given to `new Regex(...)` and the static methods of `Regex`, in which a combining mark follows another character.

no-missing-references.description: An attribute that refers to an `id` (`for`, `aria-labelledby`, `list`, `headers`, `form`, ...) names an id that no element of the document has.

no-missing-space-atx.description: A paragraph that starts with one to six `#` and no space reads as a heading to people but is plain text to Markdown (markdownlint MD018).

no-misused-new.description: A class method `new(): C` that returns the class, an interface `new (): I` that returns the interface, and an interface method `constructor()`.

no-multiple-main.description: A second `<main>` element that is not `hidden`: a page has one main landmark.

no-namespace.description: A `namespace` or `module Name` declaration (not `declare module "x"` or `declare global`), except in a `.d.ts` file.

no-nested-onbuild.description: An ONBUILD whose instruction is ONBUILD, FROM or MAINTAINER.

no-nested-style-tag.description: Svelte's `no-nested-style-tag` (eslint-plugin-svelte). Only the top-level `<style>` is compiled as CSS.

no-non-null-asserted-optional-chain.description: A non-null assertion on an optional chain (`a?.b!`, `(a?.b)!`).

no-object-in-text-mustaches.description: Svelte's `no-object-in-text-mustaches` (eslint-plugin-svelte). An object, array, function or class written in `{ }` among text. Read from the first token of the expression, so an arrow function is not found.

no-octal.description: A number that starts with `0` and another digit (`017`, `08`).

no-octal-values.description: A plain `0755` (octal to YAML 1.1 parsers, decimal 755 to YAML 1.2) or `0o755` (octal to YAML 1.2, a string to YAML 1.1). Quoted and tagged scalars are not checked. No fix: the intended value is not known.

no-plain-text-password.description: A `[string]` parameter whose name contains `password`, `passphrase` or `cred`.

no-print.description: A call of one of the `calls` that write to the console (ruff T201 and T203), unless an argument matching `redirect` sends the output elsewhere and none matching `console` sends it back to the console; a language lists its calls and the two argument patterns in its grammar's `rule` row.

console.description: An argument that sends the output to the console

redirect.description: An argument that sends the output elsewhere

no-prototype-builtins.description: `obj.hasOwnProperty(k)`, `isPrototypeOf` and `propertyIsEnumerable` called on an object that may not inherit them; use `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, k)`.

no-raw-special-elements.description: Svelte's `no-raw-special-elements` (eslint-plugin-svelte). `<head>`, `<body>`, `<window>`, `<document>`, `<element>` and `<options>` are plain elements in Svelte; the special ones are `<svelte:head>` and so on.

no-redundant-for.description: A `<label>` has a `for` that names a control inside it, which the label already labels.

no-redundant-role.description: An element with a native role (`<nav>` is `navigation`, `<button>` is `button`) does not need a `role` that says the same.

no-redundant-target-platform.description: A FROM with `--platform=$TARGETPLATFORM`, which is what it does without the option.

no-regex-spaces.description: Two or more spaces outside a character class in the string given to `new Regex(...)` and the static methods of `Regex`.

no-region-in-body.description: A `#region` inside a block (a method, accessor or lambda body, or any block in one); regions belong between members. No fix.

no-regions.description: `#region` hides code behind a label. Reported on every `#region` outside a block (a region inside a block is `no-region-in-body`'s), in disabled `#if` branches too; no fix, because removing a pair is a judgment call.

no-require-imports.description: `require(...)` of the global `require` (not one the file declares itself) and `import x = require(...)`.

no-returns-on-void.description: A `<returns>` on a method or delegate that returns `void`. The fix removes the element with its line when it is alone on it.

no-reversed-links.description: Link syntax written the wrong way round, `(text)[url]` (markdownlint MD011), at the start of a paragraph or after a blank. Reported on the paragraph; no fix, because `(text)[url]` may be meant literally.

no-secret-in-env.description: An ARG or ENV whose name contains `api_key`, `client_key`, `password`, `private`, `secret`, `token` or `username`, or is a well-known credential variable. Build secrets belong in `--mount=type=secret`.

no-self-assign.description: A plain or logical assignment whose two sides are the same tokens, `a = a`, `a.b = a.b` or `@a ||= @a` (ESLint no-self-assign, RuboCop Lint/SelfAssignment).

operators.description: The assignment operators that store the right side as it is

no-self-closing.description: `<div />` is a start tag in HTML: the browser ignores the slash and the element stays open. Void elements (see `void-style`), `<svg>` and `<math>` are left alone.

no-self-compare.description: An equality or comparison whose two sides are the same tokens: the result never changes (ESLint no-self-compare, ruff PLR0124, Sonar S1764). `x != x` as an `isNaN` test is reported too.

no-shadow-restricted-names.description: A variable, function, parameter or class named `NaN`, `Infinity`, `undefined`, `eval` or `arguments` (`var undefined;` without a value is left alone).

no-space-in-code.description: A code span that starts or ends with a space (markdownlint MD038). A span with a space on both sides of a backtick-led or backtick-ended content is allowed.

no-space-in-links.description: Link text that starts or ends with a space (markdownlint MD039).

no-sparse-arrays.description: A hole in an array literal (`[1, , 2]`), reported at its comma.

no-style-tag.description: A `<style>` element inlines styling that an external stylesheet shares between pages. A `<style>` inside a `<template>` is allowed.

no-target-blank.description: The page opened by `target="_blank"` can reach this page through `window.opener` (old browsers) and gets the referrer; both `noopener` and `noreferrer` are required, as in eslint-plugin-svelte's `no-target-blank` and eslint-plugin-vue's `no-template-target-blank`. Links to a scheme or host and computed links (`{href}`, `bind:href`, `:href`) count.

no-this-alias.description: `const self = this` and `self = this` (destructuring `this` is allowed).

no-throw-generic.description: A `raise` or `throw` of one of the generic `types`, itself or a call of it, which callers cannot tell from any other error (ruff TRY002, RuboCop Lint/RaiseException). A language lists the types in its grammar's `rule` row.

no-trailing-punctuation.description: A heading that ends with `.`, `,`, `;`, `:` or `!` (or the full-width forms) reads as a sentence, not a title (markdownlint MD026). `?` is allowed.

no-trailing-whitespace.description: Spaces or tabs at the end of a line.

no-typename-prefix.description: A field of an object or interface type starts with the name of the type (`type User { userId: ID }`); the type already says it (case ignored). No fix: renaming a field changes the schema.

no-undefined-alias.description: An alias names an anchor that is not defined earlier in the same document.

no-unexpected-multiline.description: `[`, `(` or a template at the start of a line right after an expression, which continues it (`a\n[b]` is a property access, not two statements).

no-unit-return.description: A function with a block body that declares `: Unit` (ktlint no-unit-return).

no-unknown-elements.description: An element name that HTML does not define, custom elements (`<my-element>`) included. Everything inside `<svg>` and `<math>` is left alone.

no-unknown-style-directive-property.description: Svelte's `no-unknown-style-directive-property` (eslint-plugin-svelte). Custom properties (`style:--x`) and vendor-prefixed ones pass. The property table is the CSS language's.

no-unnecessary-type-constraint.description: A type parameter constrained to `any` or `unknown`.

no-unneeded-base-prefix.description: `base.M()` or `base[i]` where the type does not override the member, so `this` binds to the same one. The fix writes `this`.

no-unneeded-ternary.description: A conditional expression whose two arms are boolean literals: `a ? true : false` is `!!a`, `a ? false : true` is `!a`.

no-unsafe-finally.description: `return`, `throw`, and a `break` or `continue` that leaves the block, in a `finally` block: they override the `try`'s own outcome.

no-unsafe-function-type.description: The global type `Function` as a type name, `extends` or `implements` target.

no-unsafe-negation.description: `!a in b` and `!a instanceof B` negate `a`, not the test.

no-unused-anchors.description: An anchor that no alias refers to. The fix removes the anchor, which changes nothing about the data.

no-use-v-else-with-v-for.description: Vue's `no-use-v-else-with-v-for` (eslint-plugin-vue). Put the `v-for` on a child or a wrapping `<template>`.

no-use-v-if-with-v-for.description: Vue's `no-use-v-if-with-v-for` (eslint-plugin-vue). Filter the list in a computed value, or move the `v-if` to a wrapping `<template>`.

no-useless-catch.description: A `catch` that only rethrows its error.

no-useless-escape.description: A backslash in a string, template or regex that escapes nothing special (`"\d"`, `/\-/`).

no-useless-expression.description: An expression statement that is only a name, a literal, a member access or an operator expression: it is evaluated and thrown away (ESLint no-unused-expressions, ruff B018). Which kinds of expression have no effect of their own is the grammar's `#pure` tag.

no-v-html.description: Vue's `no-v-html` (eslint-plugin-vue). Render the text with `{{ }}`, or sanitize it first.

no-void-end-tag.description:
A void element (`
`, ``, ...) has no content and no end tag; the browser ignores `
`.

no-wildcard-imports.description: An import of every name of a package or module, `import a.b.*;` or `from a import *` (Checkstyle AvoidStarImport, ktlint no-wildcard-imports, ruff F403).

no-wrapper-object-types.description: The global types `BigInt`, `Boolean`, `Number`, `Object`, `String` and `Symbol` as type names.

none-comparison.description: A comparison of a value to `None` with `==` or `!=`.

not-in-test.description: A membership test negated in front of the expression (`not a in b`).

not-is-test.description: An identity test negated in front of the expression (`not a is b`).

npm-pin-versions.description: An npm install package without a version.

null-comparison.description: `= NULL`, `<> NULL` or `!= NULL`, which is never true: use `IS NULL` or `IS NOT NULL` (sqlfluff CV05).

null-comparison-side.description: A `-eq`, `-ne` (or case variant) comparison with `$null` on the right.

nullable-shorthand.description: `int?` instead of `Nullable<int>` or `System.Nullable<int>`. Name-based: a type of your own called `Nullable` is reported too. Not reported in `using` aliases, `nameof`, `typeof(Nullable<>)` and before a member access (`Nullable<int>.Equals`).

number-max-precision.description: A number with more decimal places than the `max` option.

max.description: The most decimal places a number may have.

numeric-user-id.description: A USER that is a name rather than a numeric id (a variable is accepted).

oneof-lower-snake-case.description: A oneof name that is not lower_snake_case (buf lint ONEOF_LOWER_SNAKE_CASE).

open-file-without-with.description: A call of `open` (or of `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile` and the like) that is not the context of a `with`, not returned and not given to `enter_context`.

optional-annotation.description: A `typing.Optional[...]` subscript, for a target version that has `X | Y` (3.10).

os-error-alias.description: `EnvironmentError`, `IOError`, `WindowsError`, `mmap.error`, `os.error`, `select.error` or `socket.error` in an `except` clause or a `raise`.

outdated-version-block.description: A test of `sys.version_info` against a version older than the target's, or of `sys.version_info[0]` against a number: the result is always the same.

package-defined.description: A file without a `package` statement (buf lint PACKAGE_DEFINED).

package-lower-snake-case.description: A package whose components are not lower_snake_case (buf lint PACKAGE_LOWER_SNAKE_CASE).

package-name.description: A package whose name has an uppercase letter or an underscore (ktlint package-name).

package-version-suffix.description: A package whose last component is not `v1`, `v1test...`, `v1alpha1`, `v1beta1` or `v1p1alpha1` (`v1beta` too; buf lint PACKAGE_VERSION_SUFFIX).

parameter-assignment.description: A parameter is assigned a new value (Checkstyle ParameterAssignment). No fix.

parentheses-as-grouped-expression.description: A space between a method name and the `(` of its only argument (`puts (1 + 2) * 3`) (RuboCop Lint/ParenthesesAsGroupedExpression).

percent-format-expected-mapping.description: A `%` format with `%(name)s` placeholders applied to a tuple, list or set.

percent-format-expected-sequence.description: A `%` format with several positional placeholders applied to a dict.

percent-format-extra-named-arguments.description: A `%` format applied to a dict with keys no placeholder names.

percent-format-invalid-format.description: A `"..." % x` whose format string does not parse.

percent-format-missing-argument.description: A `%` format with named placeholders the dict does not have.

percent-format-positional-count-mismatch.description: A `%` format whose placeholders and values differ in number.

percent-format-star-requires-sequence.description: A `%` format with a `*` width or precision applied to a dict.

percent-format-unsupported-format-charac.description: A `%` format with a conversion character the language does not know.

phony-declared.description: A target with no recipe that is not declared `.PHONY` (checkmake `phonydeclared`); targets that start with a `.` are special and skipped.

pip-pin-versions.description: A pip install package without a version.

pipefail-shell.description: A RUN with a pipe in a stage whose SHELL instruction does not set pipefail.

possible-null-dereference.description: A member or element access on an expression the compiler's nullable analysis says may be null. Only code under `#nullable enable` is checked. Off by default: the compiler reports the same thing as CS8602.

post-condition-loop.description: A `begin ... end while cond` or `until` loop, which behaves unlike the other loops (RuboCop Lint/Loop).

prefer-as-const.description: A literal type that repeats the literal it is given to (`let a: 'a' = 'a'`, `'a' as 'a'`, `<'a'>'a'`); write `as const`.

prefer-button.description: A `<button>` can hold markup and is styled with CSS like any element; `<input type="button">` cannot.

prefer-const.description: A `let` variable that is written once, in the scope that declares it, where the write could be its declaration (an initializer, a `for-in` / `for-of` head, or an assignment statement of the same block). A destructuring assignment to members, parameters or outer names is left alone, as is the `let` of a `for (;;)` head.

prefer-native-element.description: A `role` that a native element already has (`main`, `navigation`, `button`, `list`, ...) on an element that is not that one needs scripting and styling the native element comes with.

prefer-rest-params.description: `arguments` in an ordinary function, except as the object of `arguments.name`.

prefer-spread.description: `f.apply(undefined, args)` and `o.m.apply(o, args)` with an `args` that is not an array literal.

prefer-tbody.description: A `<tr>` directly in `<table>` is moved into an implied `<tbody>` by the browser; write it.

presentation-role-style.description: `none` and `presentation` are synonyms; `none` is the one ARIA 1.2 prefers.

printf-string-formatting.description: A `"..." % x` whose format string and values pair up (a tuple of as many values, a dict for named fields, or one value for one field).

printf-variable-format.description: A `printf` whose format string contains an expansion and no `%`.

property-allowed-list.description: A property that is not in the `list` option (names, or `/regex/`). Custom properties are left out; an empty list allows everything.

property-disallowed-list.description: A property that is in the `list` option (names, or `/regex/`). Custom properties are left out.

property-no-deprecated.description: A deprecated property (`clip`, `word-wrap`, `grid-gap`, the `box-*` of the old flexbox, ...).

property-no-unknown.description: A property that no CSS specification lists. Vendor-prefixed and custom properties, descriptors of `@font-face` and the like, and names with interpolation or SCSS and Less variables are left out.

property-no-vendor-prefix.description: A vendor-prefixed property that autoprefixer knows the standard property of.

property-summary-matches-accessors.description: A property summary starts with "Gets", "Sets" or "Gets or sets" ("Gets a value indicating whether" and so on for `bool`), as the property's accessors reachable from outside the type say. The type is read from the declaration (`bool`, `Boolean`, `System.Boolean`). The fix replaces the start of the text and lower-cases what follows.

property-summary-omits-restricted-access.description: A property summary says "Gets or sets" while one of the accessors is not reachable from outside the type (`private set`, `internal get` on a public property). The fix replaces the start of the text with the one that matches the visible accessor.

qualify-namespace-usings.description: A `using` directive inside a namespace whose name is not written fully qualified (it resolves relative to the enclosing namespace). The fix writes the full name, unless it has type arguments.

quote-array-element.description: An unquoted `$var` or `${var}` among the elements of an array assignment is split into words and globbed.

quote-at-expansion.description: An unquoted `$@` or `${array[@]}` in a command's arguments.

quote-command-substitution.description: An unquoted `$(...)` or backtick substitution in a command's arguments is split into words and globbed.

quote-in-quotes.description: A word of two double-quoted strings with unquoted text between them, as `"a"b"c"`.

quote-star-expansion.description: An unquoted `$*` or `${array[*]}` in a command's arguments.

quote-variable.description: An unquoted `$var` or `${var}` in a command's arguments is split into words and globbed. Does not know which variables hold only a number or a single word.

quoted-annotation.description: A quoted name in a parameter, return or variable annotation, for a target version that does not evaluate annotations (3.14).

quoted-strings.description: Which strings are quoted. Plain scalars that are not strings (`12`, `true`, `null`, dates, ...), block scalars and scalars tagged `!!` are never checked. `required: always` wants quotes on every string, `only_when_needed` reports quotes that change nothing (unless `extra_allowed` matches) and plain strings that `extra_required` matches, `optional` only the latter.
