Fixes: quoting a plain string and switching the quote type keep the value; removing quotes is unsafe because YAML 1.2 parsers read some strings (`1e3`) as numbers.

allow_quoted_quotes.description: Accept the other quote type when the string contains the wanted quote.

extra_allowed.description: Regular expressions; a string they match may be quoted with `only_when_needed`.

extra_required.description: Regular expressions; a string they match (searched in the value) must be quoted even with `optional` or `only_when_needed`.

quote_type.description: The quotes to use. `consistent`: the first quoted string of the file decides.

required.description: `always`: every string is quoted. `optional`: quotes are free, but must be of `quote_type`. `only_when_needed`: quotes only where the string would otherwise read as something else.

raise-exception.description: Raising `Exception` itself (`raise Exception`, `raise Exception.new`), which a plain `rescue` does not catch (RuboCop Lint/RaiseException).

raise-without-from-inside-except.description: A `raise` of an exception inside an `except` clause (nested `if`, loops, `with` and `match` included; `try`, functions and classes not) without `from`, unless it raises the name the clause bound.

redeclared-variable.description: A name declared again in the same scope (`var` twice, a `var` and a parameter, two functions). In TypeScript files declaration merging (interfaces, namespaces, a class with an interface) is allowed. Built-in globals are not checked.

redundant-pattern.description: A name pattern such as `foo` already matches files and directories called `foo` at every level, so a later `foo/` or `/foo` adds nothing (no `!` pattern in between).

redundant-return-type.description: A function with a block body declares the return type the language gives it anyway (`: Unit`). The fix leaves out the colon and the type.

redundant-string-coercion.description: `to_s` on the last expression of a `#{...}` and on an argument of `puts`, `print` or `warn` (RuboCop Lint/RedundantStringCoercion).

redundant-tuple-in-exception-handler.description: An `except` clause that names a tuple of one exception.

regex-flag-alias.description: `re.A`, `re.I`, `re.L`, `re.M`, `re.S`, `re.U` or `re.X`, the short names of `re.ASCII`, `re.IGNORECASE`, `re.LOCALE`, `re.MULTILINE`, `re.DOTALL`, `re.UNICODE` and `re.VERBOSE`.

remove-unused-usings.description: A `using` directive that nothing in the file needs (the compiler's hidden CS8019, IDE0005 in the SDK analyzers). Not reported in a file that has compiler errors or `#if` regions, because unresolved or inactive code could be the one using it.

require-default-prop.description: Vue's `require-default-prop` (eslint-plugin-vue). A prop that is not required, has no `default` and is not a `Boolean` is `undefined` when the parent leaves it out. With a type (`defineProps<{ a?: string }>()`) only a component that sets defaults (`withDefaults`, a props destructure) is checked, as the plugin does without type information.

require-each-key.description: Svelte's `require-each-key` (eslint-plugin-svelte). Without a key the block updates the elements in place, which keeps stale state in inputs and components and breaks transitions.

require-for-track.description: Angular's compiler error for `@for (x of xs) {` without `track`. Only in `.component.html` files.

require-prop-types.description: Vue's `require-prop-types` (eslint-plugin-vue). A prop in the array form, or an object with no `type` or `validator`.

require-sri.description: A `<script src>` or `<link rel="stylesheet" href>` without `integrity` runs or applies a file that changed on its server (a CDN) without the page noticing.

require-yield.description: A generator function with a body and no `yield`.

required-providers.description: A `terraform` block with no `required_providers` block (tflint terraform_required_providers, in the file that has the block: the rule does not know the other files of the module).

required-version.description: A `terraform` block with no `required_version` argument (tflint terraform_required_version, in the file that has the block: the rule does not know the other files of the module).

return-in-void-context.description: `return value` in `initialize` or a setter method, whose result is ignored (RuboCop Lint/ReturnInVoidContext).

return-outside-function.description: A `return` that is not inside a function.

root-in-section.description: The `root` property stops the search for parent `.editorconfig` files, but only as a preamble pair (before the first `[section]`); inside a section editors ignore it. No fix: moving it into the preamble is the author's call.

rpc-pascal-case.description: An rpc name that is not PascalCase (buf lint RPC_PASCAL_CASE).

rpc-request-standard-name.description: The request type of an rpc is not named `<Rpc>Request` or `<Service><Rpc>Request` (buf lint RPC_REQUEST_STANDARD_NAME).

rpc-response-standard-name.description: The response type of an rpc is not named `<Rpc>Response` or `<Service><Rpc>Response` (buf lint RPC_RESPONSE_STANDARD_NAME).

rpm-pin-versions.description: A yum or dnf install package without a version.

rule-empty-line-before.description: A rule whose block spans lines needs a blank line before it, unless a comment is right before it; the first rule of a block takes none (`always-multi-line` with `first-nested` as the exception).

script-injection.description: An expression in a `run` script reads text that an attacker can choose (an issue or pull request title, a branch name, a commit message): it is pasted into the script before the shell runs, so it can inject commands. Pass it through an environment variable (`env:`) and read `"$VAR"` instead.

selection-set-depth.description: An operation or fragment nests selection sets deeper than allowed, which makes a query expensive to execute. Fragments that are spread are not followed.

max.description: The deepest allowed nesting; the operation's own selection set is level 1.

selector-anb-no-unmatchable.description: An `:nth-child()` and the like whose `An+B` can never match (`0`, `0n`, `-n`, `-2n-1`).

selector-attribute-name-disallowed-list.description: An attribute selector whose name is in the `list` option.

list.description: The disallowed attribute names: names, or `/regex/`.

selector-attribute-operator-allowed-list.description: An attribute selector operator that is not in the `list` option. An empty list allows everything.

selector-attribute-operator-disallowed-l.description: An attribute selector operator that is in the `list` option.

selector-attribute-quotes.description: An attribute selector whose value is not quoted (`[a=b]`).

selector-class-pattern.description: A class selector whose name does not match the `pattern` option (a regex). An empty pattern allows everything.

pattern.description: The regex a class name must match.

selector-combinator-allowed-list.description: A combinator (`>`, `+`, `~`, or a space for descendant) that is not in the `list` option. An empty list allows everything.

selector-combinator-disallowed-list.description: A combinator (`>`, `+`, `~`, or a space for descendant) that is in the `list` option.

selector-disallowed-list.description: The selector list of a rule (whitespace collapsed) that is in the `list` option (selectors, or `/regex/`).

selector-id-pattern.description: An id selector whose name does not match the `pattern` option (a regex). An empty pattern allows everything.

pattern.description: The regex an id name must match.

selector-max-attribute.description: A selector with more attribute selectors than the `max` option.

max.description: The most attribute selectors a selector may have.

selector-max-class.description: A selector with more class selectors than the `max` option (the ones inside `:not()` and the like count).

max.description: The most classes a selector may have.

selector-max-combinators.description: A selector with more combinators (a space between compounds counts) than the `max` option.

max.description: The most combinators a selector may have.

selector-max-compound-selectors.description: A selector with more compound selectors than the `max` option.

max.description: The most compound selectors a selector may have.

selector-max-id.description: A selector with more id selectors than the `max` option.

max.description: The most ids a selector may have.

selector-max-pseudo-class.description: A selector with more pseudo-classes than the `max` option.

max.description: The most pseudo-classes a selector may have.

selector-max-type.description: A selector with more type selectors than the `max` option.

max.description: The most type selectors a selector may have.

selector-max-universal.description: A selector with more `*` than the `max` option.

max.description: The most universal selectors a selector may have.

selector-no-deprecated.description: A deprecated pseudo-class, pseudo-element or HTML or SVG element.

selector-no-qualifying-type.description: A type selector in the same compound as a class, id or attribute selector (`ul.nav`).

selector-no-vendor-prefix.description: A vendor-prefixed pseudo-class or pseudo-element that autoprefixer knows the standard one of.

selector-pseudo-class-allowed-list.description: A pseudo-class that is not in the `list` option. An empty list allows everything.

list.description: The allowed pseudo-classes, without `:`: names, or `/regex/`.

selector-pseudo-class-disallowed-list.description: A pseudo-class that is in the `list` option.

list.description: The disallowed pseudo-classes, without `:`: names, or `/regex/`.

selector-pseudo-class-no-unknown.description: A pseudo-class that is not a CSS one. Vendor-prefixed ones are left out, and the `-webkit-scrollbar` ones count after those pseudo-elements.

selector-pseudo-element-allowed-list.description: A pseudo-element that is not in the `list` option. An empty list allows everything.

list.description: The allowed pseudo-elements, without colons: names, or `/regex/`.

selector-pseudo-element-disallowed-list.description: A pseudo-element that is in the `list` option.

list.description: The disallowed pseudo-elements, without colons: names, or `/regex/`.

selector-pseudo-element-no-unknown.description: A pseudo-element that is not a CSS one. Vendor-prefixed ones are left out.

selector-type-no-unknown.description: A type selector that is not an HTML, SVG or MathML element (custom elements included). Keyframe selectors and the arguments of `:lang()`, `:nth-child()` and the like are left out.

self-alias.description: An alias that repeats the name it is given to, `a AS a` (sqlfluff AL09).

separate-attributes.description: One attribute per attribute list: `[A, B]` becomes `[A]` and `[B]`. Lists on parameters and type parameters are left alone. The fix is not offered when the list has a comment in it.

separate-field-declarations.description: One field or event per declaration: `int a, b;` becomes `int a;` and `int b;`, each with the attributes, modifiers and type of the original. The fix is not offered when the declaration has a comment in it.

service-pascal-case.description: A service name that is not PascalCase (buf lint SERVICE_PASCAL_CASE).

service-suffix.description: A service whose name does not end in `Service` (buf lint SERVICE_SUFFIX with its default suffix).

set-attr-with-constant.description: A statement `setattr(x, "name", v)` with a literal name that is an identifier.

shadowed-variable.description: A variable, parameter or function with the name of one declared in a scope around it. A function declared later in the outer scope still counts (it is hoisted), a variable declared later does not, and `var a = function a() {}` is not a shadow. In TypeScript files a type and a value of one name, and the parameters of function types, are left alone.

kinds.description: The declarations that are checked for shadowing something (empty: all).

shorthand-property-no-redundant-values.description: A `margin`, `padding`, `border-color`, `border-style`, `border-width` or `border-radius` with two, three or four values that repeat (`1px 1px` is `1px`).

single-class-per-file.description: A file holds one class or record: every later one is reported, more parts of the first class (when it is partial) excepted. Structs, interfaces, enums and delegates are not counted. No fix.

single-cmd.description: A second CMD in one stage.

single-entrypoint.description: A second ENTRYPOINT in one stage.

single-healthcheck.description: A second HEALTHCHECK in one stage.

single-namespace-per-file.description: A file declares one namespace: every later one, nested ones included, is reported. No fix.

single-title.description: A document has more than one top-level heading (markdownlint MD025). The second and later `h1` are reported.

sorted-array-values.description: The items of a sequence of only strings or only numbers are not in order (ascending by default; numbers compare as numbers). Sequences of other or mixed items are skipped. The items that would have to move (the fewest) are reported and the first report carries the fix; the fix is unsafe because sequence order can be data.

blank_line_groups.description: Sort each run of entries between blank lines on its own.

compare.description: `ordinal` (code points), `case_insensitive`, or `natural` (digit runs compare as numbers: `a2` before `a10`).

min_values.description: Sequences with fewer items are not checked.

path_patterns.description: Regular expressions; only mappings (sequences) whose key path matches one are checked. The path is `a.b[0].c` (`["odd key"]` for keys that are not identifiers), empty for the root; none listed means everywhere. A TOML table counts as its header key and an array table is not indexed.

sorted-keys.description: The keys of a mapping are not in order (alphabetical by default). The keys reported are chosen by `report`, and the first report carries the fix. Comments on lines of their own stay where they are, a comment after an entry moves with it; moving a YAML anchor below its alias breaks the document, so the fix is unsafe.

blank_line_groups.description: Sort each run of entries between blank lines on its own.

compare.description: `ordinal` (code points), `case_insensitive`, or `natural` (digit runs compare as numbers: `a2` before `a10`).

has_properties.description: Only mappings that have all of these keys are checked.

ignored_keys.description: Regular expressions; matching keys stay where they are and are not compared.

min_keys.description: Mappings with fewer keys are not checked.

order.description: Keys that come first, in this order; the rest follow in the configured order.

path_patterns.description: Regular expressions; only mappings (sequences) whose key path matches one are checked. The path is `a.b[0].c` (`["odd key"]` for keys that are not identifiers), empty for the root; none listed means everywhere. A TOML table counts as its header key and an array table is not indexed.

report.description: Which keys are reported. `moved`: the fewest keys that would have to move (eslint-plugin-jsonc). `misplaced`: every key that sorts before one above it (yamllint).

split-command-output.description: An unquoted `$(...)` among the elements of an array assignment is split into words and globbed.

static-join.description: `"sep".join([a, b])` of a list or tuple written out in the call, which an f-string says directly.

string-dot-format-extra-named-arguments.description: A `.format` call with keywords no field names.

string-dot-format-extra-positional-argum.description: A `.format` call with positional arguments no field uses.

string-dot-format-invalid-format.description: A `"...".format(...)` whose string does not parse.

string-dot-format-missing-arguments.description: A `.format` call without an argument for a field.

string-literal-equality.description: `==` or `!=` with a string literal as an operand compares references (Checkstyle StringLiteralEquality).

struct-new-override.description: A `Struct.new` member that has the name of a method of `Struct` (`:hash`, `:size`, `:count`) (RuboCop Lint/StructNewOverride).

subprocess-run-without-check.description: A call of `subprocess.run` with no `check` keyword (and no `**kwargs`).

suppression-justification.description: `SuppressMessage` needs a `Justification` that says something: not missing, `null`, empty, blank or `"<Pending>"`. Matches the attribute by name. No fix.

svg-focusable.description: Internet Explorer 11 and old Edge make every `<svg>` focusable unless it says `focusable="false"`.

syntax-specified.description: A file without `syntax = ...;` or `edition = ...;`, which makes it proto2 (buf lint SYNTAX_SPECIFIED).

test-and-or.description: A `[ ]` test that joins conditions with `-a` or `-o`.

test-exit-status.description: A test that compares `$?` with a number.

test-grep-output.description: A `[[ ]]` or `[ -n ]` / `[ -z ]` test of the output of a pipeline or command that ends in `grep`.

text-content.description: A `<button>` with no text, no image with an `alt`, no `<svg>` and no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` has no name; a `title` does not count.

timestamp-expanded.description: A variable whose value runs `date` and that is not simply expanded (`:=`, `::=`): every use runs `date` again and the values differ within one build (checkmake `timestampexpanded`).

trap-expands-now.description: A `trap` whose double-quoted command contains an expansion.

triple-slash-reference.description: A `/// <reference path="x" />` before the first statement, and a `/// <reference types="x" />` for a module the file imports.

tuple-element-names-in-signatures.description: A tuple type in the signature of a method, constructor, property, indexer, conversion operator or delegate whose elements have no names. Overrides and implementations of interface members are left alone (their names are not the member's to choose). No fix.

type-alias-annotation.description: `X: TypeAlias = ...`, for a target version with the `type` statement (3.12).

type-check-without-type-error.description: A branch tested with `isinstance`, `issubclass` or `callable` that raises a builtin exception other than `TypeError` (and `NotImplementedError`).

type-comparison.description: A comparison with `==` or `!=` where a side is `type(x)` or a builtin class (the builtin, not a name that shadows it).

type-var-name-variance.description: A `TypeVar` with `covariant=True` whose name does not end with `_co`, or with `contravariant=True` and a name that does not end with `_contra`.

typed-variables.description: A `variable` block with no `type` argument (tflint terraform_typed_variables).

unassigned-variable.description: A lower case variable that the file reads and never assigns, reads with `read`, `getopts`, `local` or a `for` loop, or guards with a default (`${name:-x}`). Names with an upper case letter are the environment's and are left alone.

undefined-export.description: A name in `__all__` that the module does not bind.

undefined-local-with-import-star-usage.description: A name that no scope binds in a file that has a star import.

undefined-local-with-nested-import-star-.description: A star import in a function or class.

undefined-variable.description: A name that no scope declares, that is not a global of ES2026 (or, in a `.cjs` file, `require`, `module`, `exports` and `global`) and that is not in the `globals` option. `typeof x` and JSX tags are left alone.

globals.description: Names the environment declares (ESLint's `languageOptions.globals`), such as `window` or `console`.

underscore-prefixed-variable-used.description: A variable whose name starts with `_`, which says it is unused, is read (RuboCop Lint/UnderscorePrefixedVariableName). No fix.

union-annotation.description: A `typing.Union[...]` subscript, for a target version that has `X | Y` (3.10).

union-distinct.description: A `UNION` that names neither `DISTINCT` nor `ALL` (sqlfluff AM02).

unique-fragment-name.description: Two fragments of a document have the same name; a spread cannot tell which one it means. Checked within the file.

unique-landmark.description: Landmarks of one kind (`<nav>`, `<aside>`, or an element with the same landmark `role`) that a screen reader user cannot tell apart: with several of them, each needs an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` that no other has.

unique-operation-name.description: Two operations of a document have the same name; a server cannot tell which to run and tools that key on the name (caches, persisted queries) collide. Checked within the file.

unique-targets.description: A target defined by more than one rule, which merges prerequisites and overrides recipes (checkmake `uniquetargets`). Double-colon rules, `.PHONY` and the targets of `ignore` are skipped.

ignore.description: Targets that may be defined more than once.

unit-allowed-list.description: A unit (`%` included) that is not in the `list` option, in values and at-rule preludes. An empty list allows everything.

unit-disallowed-list.description: A unit (`%` included) that is in the `list` option, in values and at-rule preludes.

unit-no-unknown.description: A unit that is not a CSS unit, in values and `@media` preludes. `x` counts only in `image-set()`, `image-resolution` and `resolution` media features.

unknown-needs.description: `needs` names a job that the workflow does not define.

unknown-property.description: A property name that is not an EditorConfig or .NET (`dotnet_*`, `csharp_*`, `visual_basic_*`, `dotnet_diagnostic.<ID>.severity`, naming rule) property but is one typo away from one: the setting is silently ignored. Names of other tools (`resharper_*`, `ij_*`) are left alone. Known properties and values: `crates/lang-editorconfig/data/properties.txt`.

strict.description: Also report `dotnet_*`, `csharp_*` and `visual_basic_*` names that are close to no known property (the list may lag behind new .NET options).

unknown-rule-in-directive.description: A comment that disables a rule of another tool (the grammar's `suppress directive` markers) by a `Group/Name` whose group the tool does not have, such as an extension that is not loaded (the grammar's `suppress directive-group` rows list the groups there are).

unnecessary-collection-call.description: `dict()`, `list()` or `tuple()` with no arguments (`dict` with keyword arguments only).

unnecessary-placeholder.description: A `pass` or `...` statement in a body of two statements or more.

unquoted-pattern.description: A `==`, `!=` or `=` in `[[ ]]` whose right side is an unquoted expansion.

unreachable-code.description: A statement that can never run: after `return`, `throw`, `break` or `continue`, after an `if`/`else` or `try` that always jumps, or after a loop that never ends. Only the first statement of a run is reported. Where the language has a flow layer (C#) it also covers constant conditions and calls that do not return (`does_not_return` in `semantics:`). Hoisted declarations and empty statements are left out. Removing the statement is offered as an editor quick fix only, because unreachable code usually signals a bug.

non_returning_calls.description: With a flow layer, treat the code after a call that never returns (`[DoesNotReturn]`, `does_not_return` in `semantics:`) as unreachable. A compiler does not, so turn this off to report exactly what it reports.

unrecognized-char-ref.description: A named character reference in text (`&name;`) that HTML does not define. Numeric references and references in attribute values are not checked.

unsafe-numbers.description: A number that a double-precision parser (JavaScript, most JSON libraries) cannot hold: an integer beyond 2^53 - 1, a value that overflows to infinity, underflows to zero or is subnormal.

unsorted-dunder-all.description: An `__all__` list or tuple of strings out of order: constants (upper case) first, then classes (capitalized), then the rest, each in natural order.

unsorted-dunder-slots.description: A `__slots__` list or tuple of strings out of natural order.

unsorted-imports.description: A block of imports that differs from the isort layout (ruff's defaults): sections of future, standard library, third-party, first-party and relative imports, `import x` before `from x import y`, names in natural order without regard to case, members as constants, classes, then variables, one statement for each module, lines over 88 columns in parentheses, one blank line between sections and after the block (two before a definition at module level). A folder or file next to the file, in the project root or in its `src` folder, is first-party.

force_sort_within_sections.description: Sort `import x` and `from x import y` together by module instead of the plain imports first.

line_width.description: A `from` import over this many columns is wrapped in parentheses, one member to a line.

sections.description: The sections of the block in the order they are written; a section left out comes last.

untagged-base-image.description: A FROM image with neither a tag nor a digest, which builds on whatever `latest` is. `scratch`, a variable and an earlier stage's name are fine.

unused-annotation.description: A local variable annotated without a value and never read.

unused-assignment.description: A value is stored in a local variable and no path reads it before it is overwritten or the variable goes out of scope (a dead store). Variables that are captured or whose address is taken are not checked; a variable that is never read at all is reported by `unused-variable` instead. Overlaps the SDK analyzer IDE0059 (unnecessary assignment).

unused-block-argument.description: A block parameter that the block never reads (RuboCop Lint/UnusedBlockArgument). Names that start with `_` and empty blocks are left alone. No fix.

unused-cte.description: A common table expression that nothing in the `WITH` statement refers to (sqlfluff ST03).

unused-declarations.description: A variable, local value or data source that nothing in the same file refers to (tflint terraform_unused_declarations, within one file: a module that uses its variables in other files needs the rule off or those files in one).

unused-import.description: An import whose name the file does not use (Checkstyle UnusedImports, ktlint no-unused-imports). Imports with `*` are not checked, and a name in a doc comment counts as a use where the language has doc comments. No fix: removing an import can change which declaration a name means.

unused-local-variable.description: A local variable that is never read: it is declared, and perhaps assigned, and that is all (Checkstyle UnusedLocalVariable, RuboCop Lint/UselessAssignment). No fix.

unused-method-argument.description: A method parameter that the method never reads (RuboCop Lint/UnusedMethodArgument). Names that start with `_`, empty methods and methods that only raise NotImplementedError are left alone. No fix.

unused-parameter.description: A parameter that is never read. By default only the parameters after the last one that is read are reported; the parameters of setters and signatures and the properties a constructor declares are used.

args.description: Which parameters are checked: those after the last one that is read, all of them, or none.

ignore_pattern.description: A regex for the names that are not checked (ESLint's `argsIgnorePattern`).

unused-private-member.description: A private field, method, property or event that no file of the project uses (`analysis: deep`). Members with attributes, overrides, interface implementations, `extern` and `partial` methods are left alone, and so are the private                   methods named in `reflection_methods` of a type derived from one of                   `reflection_base_types` (a framework calls them by reflection; the `csharp/unity`                   preset lists Unity's). Overlaps the SDK analyzers IDE0051 (unused private member) and IDE0052 (unread private member).

reflection_base_types.description: Names of base classes whose derived types are called by a framework                           through reflection (with `reflection_methods`). A base is matched by its                           simple name anywhere up the inheritance chain, also when the project                           does not load its assembly.

reflection_methods.description: Names of private methods that count as used in a type derived from                           one of `reflection_base_types`.

unused-unpacked-variable.description: A name of a tuple target in a function that the function never reads (not `_` names, not in functions that call `locals()`).

unused-variable.description: A local variable or catch variable that is never used (the compiler's CS0168), or is only assigned constants and never read (CS0219). Variables captured by lambdas or local functions count as used. Off by default: the compiler already warns (CS0168, CS0219).

upper-ell.description: An integer literal that ends in a lower case `l` (Checkstyle UpperEll).

use-before-define.description: A reference that comes before the declaration of what it names in the source (function declarations included), or runs while the variable is being initialized. References in types are left alone.

use-isnan.description: A comparison with `NaN`, or `NaN` as the discriminant or a case test of a `switch`; use `Number.isNaN`.

use-lambda.description: A lambda instead of an anonymous method. The fix is offered when the anonymous method has a parameter list and no comment before its body; `delegate { }` without one converts to delegate types with any parameters, so it has no fix.

use-literal-suffix.description: A numeric literal cast to `long`, `ulong`, `uint`, `float`, `double` or `decimal` when the literal's own type differs: `(long)1` is `1L`. Not reported for hexadecimal and binary literals cast to a floating-point type, which have no suffix.

use-string-empty.description: `string.Empty` instead of `""` (or `@""`). Not reported where a constant is required: `const`, attribute arguments, default parameter values, `case` labels and patterns.

use-tuple-syntax.description: `ValueTuple<int, int>` and `ValueTuple.Create(a, b)` where tuple syntax `(int, int)` and `(a, b)` is available (not inside an expression tree). The fix is offered for types and `ValueTuple.Create` calls.

useless-access-modifier.description: A bare `private`, `protected`, `public` or `module_function` that repeats the visibility already in force, or is followed by no method definition (RuboCop Lint/UselessAccessModifier).

useless-cat.description: A pipeline that starts with `cat file`.

useless-echo.description: An `echo` whose only argument is a command substitution.

useless-import-alias.description: `import a as a` or `from m import a as a`.

useless-method-definition.description: A method whose whole body is a bare `super` (RuboCop Lint/UselessMethodDefinition).

useless-object-inheritance.description: A class with the builtin `object` as a base.

useless-semicolon.description: A `;` at the end of a line.

using-order.description: `using` directives of a file or namespace are out of order: System first (`system_first`), names in alphabetical order (`compare`), and with the options `static_position` and `alias_position` set to `after`, `using static` directives after the plain ones and aliases after those, each group sorted. `global using` and `using unsafe` stay where they are, and a list restarts at a directive that has a preprocessor directive in front of it (the fix leaves such lists alone). Comments on lines of their own stay where they are; a comment after a directive moves with it. Overlaps the SDK analyzers' `dotnet_sort_system_directives_first` .editorconfig key.

alias_position.description: `after`: alias directives come after all other usings, sorted by alias name; `keep`: they stay where they are.

compare.description: `ordinal` compares code points; `culture` ignores case (and puts punctuation before digits before letters, a lower-case name before an upper-case one that is otherwise equal); `culture_ignore_case` leaves names that differ only in case in their order.

static_position.description: `after`: `using static` directives come after the plain usings, sorted (System ones first with `system_first`); `keep`: they stay where they are.

system_first.description: Put `System` and `System.*` before the other namespaces.

v-for-key.description: Vue's `require-v-for-key` (eslint-plugin-vue). A `v-for` without a `:key` (or `v-bind:key`) makes Vue patch the elements in place, which keeps stale state in inputs and components. On a `<template>` or `<slot>` the key goes on the child elements; components are left to `valid-v-for`.

v-on-event-hyphenation.description: Vue's `v-on-event-hyphenation` (eslint-plugin-vue). Applies to components (a tag in PascalCase or with a hyphen), not to HTML and SVG elements.

valid-id.description: An `id` that is empty, has whitespace, begins with a digit or has other characters is valid HTML5 but breaks CSS selectors and some scripts.

valid-typeof.description: `typeof x` compared with a string that is not a type name, or with `undefined`.

valid-v-else.description: Vue's `valid-v-else` (eslint-plugin-vue). Only comments and blank space may sit between the elements of a chain.

valid-v-else-if.description: Vue's `valid-v-else-if` (eslint-plugin-vue). Only comments and blank space may sit between the elements of a chain.

valid-v-for.description: Vue's `valid-v-for` (eslint-plugin-vue), the syntax of the directive. A missing `:key` is `v-for-key`.

valid-v-if.description: Vue's `valid-v-if` (eslint-plugin-vue). An element with `v-else-if` or `v-else` continues an earlier chain.

valid-v-model.description: Vue's `valid-v-model` (eslint-plugin-vue). A file input has no value Vue can set; listen to `@change` instead.

valid-v-on.description: Vue's `valid-v-on` (eslint-plugin-vue). `@click="go"`; `@click.prevent` alone is fine, `@click` is not.

valid-v-slot.description: Vue's `valid-v-slot` (eslint-plugin-vue). `<template #name="props">`; a plain element such as `<div>` cannot receive a slot.

value-no-vendor-prefix.description: A vendor-prefixed keyword or function that autoprefixer knows the standard value of.

verbose-raise.description: `raise e` in the `except ... as e` clause, where a bare `raise` keeps the traceback.

void-style.description:
A void element (`
`, ``, ...) has no end tag and needs no `/`; write `
`, not `
`.

wget-progress.description: A wget call with no progress, quiet or log-file flag.

workdir-absolute.description: A WORKDIR whose path is not absolute (a leading `/`, a drive letter or a variable).

yield-outside-function.description: A `yield`, `yield from` or `await` outside a function.

yum-clean.description: yum install with no yum clean all after it.

zip-without-explicit-strict.description: A call of `zip` with several arguments (or a starred one) and no `strict` keyword, for Python 3.10 and later.

zypper-clean.description: zypper install with no zypper clean after it.

zypper-pin-versions.description: A zypper install package without a version.

description: Configuration of Sudsy, the formatter and linter for source and data files.

analysis.description: Analysis depth for rules: fast (syntax only), standard (within each file), deep (adds project scope).

bracket_same_line.description: Put the `>` of a multi-line start tag at the end of the last attribute's line.

embedded_language_formatting.description: Format the code of `<script>` and `<style>` and of `style`, `srcset` and event-handler attributes with the formatter of its language (`auto`, Prettier's `embeddedLanguageFormatting`), or keep it as written (`off`). Code that does not parse, or of a language that is not installed, is kept either way.

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

single_attribute_per_line.description: Put every attribute of a tag that has several on its own line.

whitespace_sensitivity.description: Whether whitespace between inline elements and text is significant: `css` follows each element's CSS display, `strict` treats every element as inline, `ignore` as block.

semantics.description: Facts about methods that the flow analyses use.

does_not_return.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

pure.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

access_modifier_outdent.description: Columns `public:`, `private:` and `protected:` are outdented from the members of their class.

align_after_open_bracket.description: Wrapped lines inside brackets line up with the first token after the bracket (`align`), continue with `continuation_indent` (`dont_align`), or always start on a new line after the bracket (`always_break`).

align_escaped_newlines.description: The backslashes of a multi-line macro: aligned at `line_width` (`right`), one blank after the longest line (`left`) or one blank after each line.

align_trailing_comments.description: Align the trailing comments of consecutive lines.

align_with_tabs.description: With `indent_style: tab`, the alignment of continuation lines uses tabs for each whole indent width and spaces for the rest.

bin_pack_arguments.description: Call arguments that do not fit on a line are filled; when false they go one per line (or all on one line).

bin_pack_parameters.description: Function parameters that do not fit on a line are filled; when false they go one per line (or all on one line).

brace_wrapping.description: Constructs whose opening brace goes on its own line: `class`, `struct`, `union`, `enum`, `function`, `namespace`, `extern`, `control` (if, for, while, switch, do, try), `case`, `else` (the `else` after a block starts a line), `catch` (the `catch` after a block starts a line), `while` (the `while` of a do loop starts a line). Empty: every brace stays on the line of its construct.

break_after_return_type.description: The function name goes on a new line after its return type: never, for declarations and definitions outside classes (`top_level`), for all, or for definitions only (`top_level_definitions`, `all_definitions`).

align_escaped_newlines.description: The backslashes of a multi-line macro: aligned at `line_width` (`right`), one blank after the longest line (`left`) or one blank after each line.

align_with_tabs.description: With `indent_style: tab`, the alignment of continuation lines uses tabs for each whole indent width and spaces for the rest.

assignment_conditional.description: A conditional (`a ? b : c`) as the value of an assignment moves below the operator when it does not fit: `always`, or `binary_test` only when its test is an operator chain.

assignment_indent.description: Levels of indentation of a value that moves below the operator of an assignment.

assignment_layout.description: Where the value after `=` (or `=>`) goes when the line is too long: `compact` moves a binary expression, a conditional or a query to the next line and leaves any other value on the line; `fluid` also moves strings, collection expressions and property initializers, and any other value whose first line does not fit after the operator (a string that spans lines stays on the operator's line; the body of an expression lambda moves below `=>`; chains `a = b = c` get layouts of their own); `break` moves every value that does not fit; `multiline` does the same except for a value with no place to break a line, which stays.

base_list_layout.description: The base list of a type (`: A, B`): `inline` keeps it on the line of the type name; `hanging` keeps it there when it fits and otherwise starts a line, with one base type per line.

binary_hug.description: A broken operator chain leaves the indentation of its continuation lines to the layout around it: `assignment` for the value of an assignment, declaration or entry, `statement` also for the value of `return` and `throw`.

binary_indent.description: Levels of indentation of the continuation lines of a broken operator chain.

binary_operator_line.description: Where an operator of a chain (`a + b + c`) that does not fit goes: `start` breaks before it and puts one operand per line; `end` keeps it at the end of the line and moves an operand down only when it does not fit (a chain that mixes node kinds breaks at every operator).

blank_after_block_kinds.description: Node kinds that get a blank line before them after a closing brace when `blank_lines_between_members` is `always`.

blank_compact_kinds.description: Node kinds of which two in a row need no blank line between them when `blank_lines_between_members` is `always`.

blank_directives_attach.description: Preprocessor directives (by their first characters) that follow an item with no blank line between and have a blank line after them (`#pragma warning disable` after a member): they belong to that item, and the blank line options add no blank line before them.

blank_directives_skip.description: Preprocessor directives (by their first characters) in front of a member or statement after which the blank line before it is the source's: the item may start after the directive, so the blank line options add none.

blank_line_after_comment.description: Blank line between the last `//` or `///` comment in front of code and that code: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops it. Comments at the start of a file and `////` comments keep theirs.

blank_line_before_comment.description: Blank line between a statement, member or switch section and a `//` comment on the lines before the next one (not `////`): `preserve` keeps the source's; `require` adds one.

blank_lines_after_block.description: Blank line after a statement, member or switch section that ends with a closing brace: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `require` adds one before the next statement, member or section.

blank_lines_between_members.description: Blank lines between the members of a type, namespace or enum: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one) and never adds one; `separate` also requires one between two members when either has a body, an attribute or a comment above it; `always` requires one between any two members of a type or namespace and between the `using` directives and what follows them, except between two fields or two `using` directives (enum members as `separate`).

brace_newline.description: Opening braces of types, members, blocks and lambdas: `all` puts each on its own line (Allman); `none` keeps it on the line of the declaration or statement.

brace_same_line.description: Elements whose opening brace stays on the line of the declaration or statement although `brace_newline` is `all`: `types`, `methods`, `properties`, `accessors`, `anonymous_methods`, `anonymous_types`, `control_blocks`, `lambdas`, `object_collection_array_initializers` (types include namespaces, methods include constructors, operators and local functions, properties include indexers and events, control blocks include `switch` statements and bare blocks).

catch_line.description: `catch` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

clause_keyword_line.description: `else`, `catch` and `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} else {`) unless a comment sits between them.

closing_paren_line.description: The `)` of a parameter, argument or attribute argument list that does not fit on one line: `own_line` puts it on a line of its own after the last item; `same_line` right after the last item.

collection_blank_lines.description: Blank lines between the elements of a collection initializer, array initializer or collection expression: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops them. The members of an object initializer keep theirs.

conditional_indent.description: Levels of indentation of the branches of a broken conditional in the `indented` layout.

conditional_layout.description: Layout of a conditional (`a ? b : c`) that does not fit: `indented` puts the branches one level below the test, each conditional a group of its own; `chained` aligns the branches after `? ` and `: ` and breaks a chain of conditionals in the `else` branch as one.

constructor_initializer_line.description: The `: base(...)` or `: this(...)` initializer of a constructor: `same_line` keeps it after the parameter list; `new_line` puts it on its own indented line.

derive_symbol_sets.description: Also parse with sets of symbols taken from the `#if` and `#elif` conditions of the file (the empty set, all symbols, then each symbol, then pairs and so on, at most 16 sets, after those of `preprocessor_symbol_sets`) until every branch has been active once, and format the branches that are inactive under `preprocessor_symbols` from those parses. A branch no set activates stays as it is.

do_while_line.description: The `while` of a `do` statement: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} while (x);`).

else_line.description: `else` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

empty_braces.description: Braces with nothing between them: `space` prints `{ }`, `tight` prints `{}`, `expanded` puts the closing brace of an empty body on the line after the opening one (initializers, and lambdas and anonymous methods, stay `{ }`).

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

finally_line.description: `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

indent_nested_binary.description: Indent the operands of a binary expression that is itself an operand of a binary expression with an operator of another precedence (`a && b || c`).

indent_switch_section_block.description: Indent a block that is the only statement of a `case` section below its label; when false the block starts at the label's indentation.

initializer_collapse.description: Initializers and collection expressions: `preserve` keeps one expanded when the source has a line break in it; `always` puts one on a single line whenever it fits.

initializer_expand.description: Initializers (and anonymous types) that fit on a line: `fit` keeps them on it; `crowded` puts one item per line when there are three or more member assignments, or two or more items one of which creates an object with an initializer.

inline_accessor_bodies.description: Keep the body of an accessor on its line (`get { return x; }`) when it is one simple statement without comments and fits; otherwise the braces go on their own lines.

label_indent.description: Indentation of a `goto` label: `no_change` keeps the indentation of the statements around it; `one_less` indents it one level less; `flush_left` puts it in column 0.

lambda_argument_hug.description: A lambda argument whose body can hang from the call's line: `last` hugs a block lambda that is the last argument; `sole` hugs a lambda (block or expression) only when it is the only argument.

member_attribute_line.description: An attribute list in front of a member, statement or type: `own_line` puts it on a line of its own; `keep` leaves one that the source writes on the same line as what it annotates there (`[SerializeField] private int speed;`).

member_chain_break_on_block.description: Break a member chain one call per line when it has an argument with a block body (a lambda or an anonymous class) even if the chain would fit: `inner` when a call other than the last has one, `any` when any call has one.

member_chain_indent.description: Levels of indentation of the lines of a broken member chain.

member_chain_keep_accesses.description: In a broken member chain an access stays on the line of the call after it (`.a.b()` is one group) instead of starting a line of its own: `always`, or `head` in the first group only (which stays on the line of the head when the head name is short or a type name).

member_chain_min_calls.description: A chain of member accesses and calls with at least this many calls is broken one call per line when it does not fit on a line (`fluent` style).

member_chain_short_head.description: A name of at most this many characters at the head of a broken member chain stays on the line of the first call (`x.foo()`); a capitalized name, `this`, `base`, `super` and a keyword type always do.

parameter_attribute_layout.description: A parameter with attribute lists: `inline` keeps them in front of the parameter;              `hanging` keeps them there when the parameter fits and otherwise puts the rest of              the parameter on an indented line below them.

preprocessor_symbol_sets.description: Further sets of conditional compilation symbols. preprocessor_symbols.description: Conditional compilation symbols (`DEBUG`, `NET8_0`) defined when parsing, which decide the active branch of `#if`. Branches that are inactive under these symbols stay as they are unless `preprocessor_symbol_sets` or `derive_symbol_sets` format them.

preserve_query_breaks.description: A query expression with a line break in the source keeps one clause per line even when it fits on a line.

preserve_single_line_blocks.description: A block written on one line (`void M() { return; }`, `get { return x; }`,              `if (a)` followed by `{ b(); }`) stays on one line, as `{ a; b; }`, when it has no comment and no label in it. preserve_single_line_statements.description: Statements written on one line stay there: `a(); b();` in a sequence, `case 1:              break;`, and a whole `if`, `while`, `for`, `foreach`, `do`, `try`, `using`, `lock`,              `fixed`, `checked` or `unsafe` statement (with its blocks) written on one line,              unless it has a comment, a `switch` or a label in it.

separate_using_groups.description: With `sort_usings`: one blank line between the System usings and the others (only with `sort_usings_system_first`).

sort_usings.description: Sort `using` directives like the `using-order` rule with `compare: culture_ignore_case`, `static_position: after` and `alias_position: after` (System first, then the others, `using static`, aliases), and join the groups: blank lines between directives go, comments above a directive move with it. `global using` directives come first, `using global::X` behind the System ones. `#if` regions stay as they are behind the sorted directives; a list with another preprocessor directive is left alone.

sort_usings_system_first.description: With `sort_usings`: `System` namespaces come before the others (`using static System.*` before other `using static`).

space_after_delegate.description: A space between `delegate` and the parameter list of an anonymous method (`delegate (int x) { }`); when false `delegate(int x) { }`.

space_after_empty_last_for_clause.description: A space before the `)` of a `for` whose last clause is empty (`for (int i = 0; i < n; )`); when false `for (int i = 0; i < n;)`.

space_between_empty_for_clauses.description: A space between the two semicolons of a `for` with an empty condition (`for (; ;)`); when false `for (;;)`.

switch_arm_layout.description: Layout of a switch expression arm: `inline` keeps `pattern => value` as one run of tokens; `assignment` lays out the value like the right-hand side of `=` (see `assignment_layout`).

trailing_commas.description: Trailing comma after the last element of initializers, collection expressions, enums and switch expressions: `preserve` keeps what the source has; `never` removes it; `multiline` adds one when the list is on several lines and removes it otherwise.

unbreakable_single_item_lists.description: Never break a list that holds one simple item: an attribute list with one attribute, a type argument list with one name, an index that is one name or literal.

wrapped_brace_line.description: Opening brace of an initializer or property pattern that is laid out on several lines: `creation` puts it on its own line for `new T { ... }` only; `all` also for an initializer nested in an assignment (`Prop = { ... }`) and for property patterns; `none` keeps it on the line of the expression.

indent_braces.description: Indent a brace that is on its own line together with the block it opens.

indent_case_labels.description: Indent `case` labels one level inside their `switch`.

indent_goto_labels.description: A goto label stands one indent left of the statements of its block; when false it starts at column 0.

indent_pp_directives.description: A preprocessor directive starts with `#` directly followed by its keyword (`none`) or keeps the blanks written after the `#` (`keep`).

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

keep_leading_blank_lines.description: Blank lines at the start of the file stay.

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

max_blank_lines.description: Largest number of blank lines kept between statements and comments.

namespace_indentation.description: Indent the contents of namespaces: `none`, only namespaces nested in another (`inner`), or `all`.

penalty_return_type.description: What a return type on a line of its own costs the layout; the higher, the longer the parameter list may wrap before the return type moves.

pointer_alignment.description: Where the `*` and `&` of a pointer or reference declarator go: next to the name (`right`), next to the type (`left`) or between them (`middle`).

short_case_labels.description: A `case` label and its simple statement are kept on one line when they fit.

short_enums.description: An enum whose body fits stays on one line.

short_functions.description: Function bodies kept on the line of the signature when they fit: `none`, `empty` (`{}` only), `inline` (functions defined in a class, and empty ones) or `all`.

short_ifs.description: An `if` with a simple statement is kept on one line when it fits: `never`, without an `else`, or with or without.

short_lambdas.description: Lambda bodies kept on the line of the lambda when they fit: `none`, `empty`, `inline` (a lambda that is an argument) or `all`.

short_loops.description: A `for`, `while` or range-for with a simple statement is kept on one line when it fits.

space_before_parens.description: A blank before the parenthesis of `if`, `for`, `while`, `switch` and `catch` (`control_statements`), before every parenthesis (`always`) or never.

spaces_before_trailing_comments.description: Blanks between the code of a line and its `//` comment.

wrap_lines.description: Break lines that are longer than `line_width`. When false, every line keeps the line breaks of the source (only indentation and spacing change).

does_not_return.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

pure.description: Qualified method names without parameter lists; every overload is covered.

accessor_blank_lines.description: Blank lines between the accessors of a property that is laid out on several lines: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops them.

assignment_conditional.description: A conditional (`a ? b : c`) as the value of an assignment moves below the operator when it does not fit: `always`, or `binary_test` only when its test is an operator chain.

assignment_indent.description: Levels of indentation of a value that moves below the operator of an assignment.

assignment_layout.description: Where the value after `=` (or `=>`) goes when the line is too long: `compact` moves a binary expression, a conditional or a query to the next line and leaves any other value on the line; `fluid` also moves strings, collection expressions and property initializers, and any other value whose first line does not fit after the operator (a string that spans lines stays on the operator's line; the body of an expression lambda moves below `=>`; chains `a = b = c` get layouts of their own); `break` moves every value that does not fit; `multiline` does the same except for a value with no place to break a line, which stays.

base_list_layout.description: The base list of a type (`: A, B`): `inline` keeps it on the line of the type name; `hanging` keeps it there when it fits and otherwise starts a line, with one base type per line.

binary_hug.description: A broken operator chain leaves the indentation of its continuation lines to the layout around it: `assignment` for the value of an assignment, declaration or entry, `statement` also for the value of `return` and `throw`.

binary_indent.description: Levels of indentation of the continuation lines of a broken operator chain.

binary_operator_line.description: Where an operator of a chain (`a + b + c`) that does not fit goes: `start` breaks before it and puts one operand per line; `end` keeps it at the end of the line and moves an operand down only when it does not fit (a chain that mixes node kinds breaks at every operator).

blank_after_block_kinds.description: Node kinds that get a blank line before them after a closing brace when `blank_lines_between_members` is `always`.

blank_compact_kinds.description: Node kinds of which two in a row need no blank line between them when `blank_lines_between_members` is `always`.

blank_directives_attach.description: Preprocessor directives (by their first characters) that follow an item with no blank line between and have a blank line after them (`#pragma warning disable` after a member): they belong to that item, and the blank line options add no blank line before them.

blank_directives_skip.description: Preprocessor directives (by their first characters) in front of a member or statement after which the blank line before it is the source's: the item may start after the directive, so the blank line options add none.

blank_line_after_comment.description: Blank line between the last `//` or `///` comment in front of code and that code: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops it. Comments at the start of a file and `////` comments keep theirs.

blank_line_before_comment.description: Blank line between a statement, member or switch section and a `//` comment on the lines before the next one (not `////`): `preserve` keeps the source's; `require` adds one.

blank_lines_after_block.description: Blank line after a statement, member or switch section that ends with a closing brace: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `require` adds one before the next statement, member or section.

blank_lines_between_members.description: Blank lines between the members of a type, namespace or enum: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one) and never adds one; `separate` also requires one between two members when either has a body, an attribute or a comment above it; `always` requires one between any two members of a type or namespace and between the `using` directives and what follows them, except between two fields or two `using` directives (enum members as `separate`).

brace_newline.description: Opening braces of types, members, blocks and lambdas: `all` puts each on its own line (Allman); `none` keeps it on the line of the declaration or statement.

brace_same_line.description: Elements whose opening brace stays on the line of the declaration or statement although `brace_newline` is `all`: `types`, `methods`, `properties`, `accessors`, `anonymous_methods`, `anonymous_types`, `control_blocks`, `lambdas`, `object_collection_array_initializers` (types include namespaces, methods include constructors, operators and local functions, properties include indexers and events, control blocks include `switch` statements and bare blocks).

catch_line.description: `catch` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

clause_keyword_line.description: `else`, `catch` and `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} else {`) unless a comment sits between them.

closing_paren_line.description: The `)` of a parameter, argument or attribute argument list that does not fit on one line: `own_line` puts it on a line of its own after the last item; `same_line` right after the last item.

collection_blank_lines.description: Blank lines between the elements of a collection initializer, array initializer or collection expression: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops them. The members of an object initializer keep theirs.

conditional_indent.description: Levels of indentation of the branches of a broken conditional in the `indented` layout.

conditional_layout.description: Layout of a conditional (`a ? b : c`) that does not fit: `indented` puts the branches one level below the test, each conditional a group of its own; `chained` aligns the branches after `? ` and `: ` and breaks a chain of conditionals in the `else` branch as one.

constructor_initializer_line.description: The `: base(...)` or `: this(...)` initializer of a constructor: `same_line` keeps it after the parameter list; `new_line` puts it on its own indented line.

derive_symbol_sets.description: Also parse with sets of symbols taken from the `#if` and `#elif` conditions of the file (the empty set, all symbols, then each symbol, then pairs and so on, at most 16 sets, after those of `preprocessor_symbol_sets`) until every branch has been active once, and format the branches that are inactive under `preprocessor_symbols` from those parses. A branch no set activates stays as it is.

do_while_line.description: The `while` of a `do` statement: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} while (x);`).

else_line.description: `else` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

empty_braces.description: Braces with nothing between them: `space` prints `{ }`, `tight` prints `{}`, `expanded` puts the closing brace of an empty body on the line after the opening one (initializers, and lambdas and anonymous methods, stay `{ }`).

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

finally_line.description: `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

indent_nested_binary.description: Indent the operands of a binary expression that is itself an operand of a binary expression with an operator of another precedence (`a && b || c`).

indent_switch_section_block.description: Indent a block that is the only statement of a `case` section below its label; when false the block starts at the label's indentation.

initializer_collapse.description: Initializers and collection expressions: `preserve` keeps one expanded when the source has a line break in it; `always` puts one on a single line whenever it fits.

initializer_expand.description: Initializers (and anonymous types) that fit on a line: `fit` keeps them on it; `crowded` puts one item per line when there are three or more member assignments, or two or more items one of which creates an object with an initializer.

inline_accessor_bodies.description: Keep the body of an accessor on its line (`get { return x; }`) when it is one simple statement without comments and fits; otherwise the braces go on their own lines.

label_indent.description: Indentation of a `goto` label: `no_change` keeps the indentation of the statements around it; `one_less` indents it one level less; `flush_left` puts it in column 0.

lambda_argument_hug.description: A lambda argument whose body can hang from the call's line: `last` hugs a block lambda that is the last argument; `sole` hugs a lambda (block or expression) only when it is the only argument.

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

member_attribute_line.description: An attribute list in front of a member, statement or type: `own_line` puts it on a line of its own; `keep` leaves one that the source writes on the same line as what it annotates there (`[SerializeField] private int speed;`).

member_chain_break_on_block.description: Break a member chain one call per line when it has an argument with a block body (a lambda or an anonymous class) even if the chain would fit: `inner` when a call other than the last has one, `any` when any call has one.

member_chain_indent.description: Levels of indentation of the lines of a broken member chain.

member_chain_keep_accesses.description: In a broken member chain an access stays on the line of the call after it (`.a.b()` is one group) instead of starting a line of its own: `always`, or `head` in the first group only (which stays on the line of the head when the head name is short or a type name).

member_chain_min_calls.description: A chain of member accesses and calls with at least this many calls is broken one call per line when it does not fit on a line (`fluent` style).

member_chain_short_head.description: A name of at most this many characters at the head of a broken member chain stays on the line of the first call (`x.foo()`); a capitalized name, `this`, `base`, `super` and a keyword type always do.

parameter_attribute_layout.description: A parameter with attribute lists: `inline` keeps them in front of the parameter;              `hanging` keeps them there when the parameter fits and otherwise puts the rest of              the parameter on an indented line below them.

preprocessor_symbol_sets.description: Further sets of conditional compilation symbols. The file is also parsed with each set (a set replaces `preprocessor_symbols`), and the `#if` branches that are inactive under `preprocessor_symbols` but active under a set are formatted from that parse. Empty (the default) leaves inactive branches as they are.

preprocessor_symbols.description: Conditional compilation symbols (`DEBUG`, `NET8_0`) defined when parsing, which decide the active branch of `#if`. Branches that are inactive under these symbols stay as they are unless `preprocessor_symbol_sets` or `derive_symbol_sets` format them.

preserve_query_breaks.description: A query expression with a line break in the source keeps one clause per line even when it fits on a line.

preserve_single_line_blocks.description: A block written on one line (`void M() { return; }`, `get { return x; }`,              `if (a)` followed by `{ b(); }`) stays on one line, as `{ a; b; }`, when it has no comment and no label in it. preserve_single_line_statements.description: Statements written on one line stay there: `a(); b();` in a sequence, `case 1:              break;`, and a whole `if`, `while`, `for`, `foreach`, `do`, `try`, `using`, `lock`,              `fixed`, `checked` or `unsafe` statement (with its blocks) written on one line,              unless it has a comment, a `switch` or a label in it.

separate_using_groups.description: With `sort_usings`: one blank line between the System usings and the others (only with `sort_usings_system_first`).

sort_usings.description: Sort `using` directives like the `using-order` rule with `compare: culture_ignore_case`, `static_position: after` and `alias_position: after` (System first, then the others, `using static`, aliases), and join the groups: blank lines between directives go, comments above a directive move with it. `global using` directives come first, `using global::X` behind the System ones. `#if` regions stay as they are behind the sorted directives; a list with another preprocessor directive is left alone.

sort_usings_system_first.description: With `sort_usings`: `System` namespaces come before the others (`using static System.*` before other `using static`).

space_after_delegate.description: A space between `delegate` and the parameter list of an anonymous method (`delegate (int x) { }`); when false `delegate(int x) { }`.

space_after_empty_last_for_clause.description: A space before the `)` of a `for` whose last clause is empty (`for (int i = 0; i < n; )`); when false `for (int i = 0; i < n;)`.

space_between_empty_for_clauses.description: A space between the two semicolons of a `for` with an empty condition (`for (; ;)`); when false `for (;;)`.

switch_arm_layout.description: Layout of a switch expression arm: `inline` keeps `pattern => value` as one run of tokens; `assignment` lays out the value like the right-hand side of `=` (see `assignment_layout`).

trailing_commas.description: Trailing comma after the last element of initializers, collection expressions, enums and switch expressions: `preserve` keeps what the source has; `never` removes it; `multiline` adds one when the list is on several lines and removes it otherwise.

unbreakable_single_item_lists.description: Never break a list that holds one simple item: an attribute list with one attribute, a type argument list with one name, an index that is one name or literal.

wrapped_brace_line.description: Opening brace of an initializer or property pattern that is laid out on several lines: `creation` puts it on its own line for `new T { ... }` only; `all` also for an initializer nested in an assignment (`Prop = { ... }`) and for property patterns; `none` keeps it on the line of the expression.
